# track3r-os user manual

> Community operating system for the Polyend Tracker hardware. Unofficial: not affiliated with or endorsed by Polyend. This is the user manual, one chapter per screen; read the chapter of the screen you are asked about.

Key notation: keys are written in code style, for example `Shift` + `F3` or hold `Instr`; `F1` to `F8` are the soft keys under the screen. If a thing is not in the manual, it is not known: say so.


---

# Installing track3r-os

Status: draft

The release file is an Intel HEX image under a `.ptf` name, which is what the Tracker's bootloader flashes, and the bootloader itself is not touched by an update. Once track3r-os runs, later updates can also be sent from a computer with `o3console.py`, and the official firmware can be put back. More testing is needed, especially of the way back to the official firmware.

> **Unofficial, at your own risk.** track3r-os is community firmware. It is not affiliated with or endorsed by Polyend. Installing it replaces the firmware in your unit. The bootloader that flashes it is separate from the firmware and is not touched by an update (`docs/hw/tracker-hardware-notes.md`, section 3), but nothing here is a guarantee. Read the whole page first.

**Current release: v1.3.1** ([release notes](../release/v1.3.1.md)). The install steps below are the ones that worked for earlier releases.

This page says what is established by observation on the maintainer's unit and by the repository's own tests. Where a step has had little testing, do it only if you accept that risk and have a way back (see [Going back](#going-back-to-the-official-firmware)).

## What a release contains

A release (GitHub, "Releases") has four files (v1.3.1):

- `track3r-os-v1.3.1.ptf`: the update file. It is the device image in Intel HEX form under a `.ptf` name, which is what the Tracker's bootloader flashes. Its name never starts with `Polyend`, so it cannot be mistaken for an official file. For a first install through the reset button you rename your copy on the card (section 1).
- `track3r-os-v1.3.1-modules.zip`: every external module: the apps, the effects, the instruments (`tb303`, `chip`, `fm`, `sid`, `sine`; they are not inside the firmware) with their licence texts, the `tracker` importer for MOD, S3M and MED, the factory presets, and the nineteen Sample Editor plugins (`.ptfx`, which go in `Effects/`).
- `track3r-os-v1.3.1-examples.zip`: demo projects, a drum kit, wavetables, an OctaMED module and the licences of the files.
- `SHA256SUMS`: the checksums of the three files. Check your download before using it: `sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS`. The release notes also give the CRC-32 that `o3console.py --update --crc` asks for.

**Unzip both zips at the root of the card.** The zips are optional for the firmware to run, but two kinds of file in them matter: the instrument modules (a project that uses the TB-303, Chip, FM or SID says **MODULE NOT ON THE CARD** without its file in `modules/instruments/`) and the importer: module import runs from `modules/importers/tracker.tmod`, and without it IMPORT of a MOD, S3M or OctaMED file says **NO IMPORTER** and changes nothing (your open project stays loaded). Keep these files on the card. Each zip's `README.txt` says what goes where.

The same image shows its version in Config, INFO (BUILD ID, for example `v1.2.0 (be2d71258138)`), on the boot screen, and in the `version` command of the USB `diag` console.

## Before you start

1. **Back up the SD card.** Copy everything on it to your computer: projects, samples, modules and the `Firmware/` folder (it holds the official image you may want to go back to). The USB update path writes only inside `Firmware/` (`platform/mk66/update/include/o3os/platform/mk66/update/path_guard.h`), but the card is what the bootloader reads, and a card is easy to damage when it is pulled and reinserted.
2. **Have the official firmware file at hand.** Official images are named `PolyendTracker_<version>.ptf`. Get one from Polyend; their pages are linked from `docs/hw/tracker-hardware-notes.md` ([how to update](https://polyend.ladesk.com/220365-How-do-I-update-Trackers-firmware), [emergency flashing](https://polyend.ladesk.com/929798-How-do-I-perform-the-emergency-flashing-procedure)). The vendor's emergency-flashing page is also where the hidden reset button used below is described.
3. **Use a normal card.** The Tracker needs a single FAT32 partition with an MBR. The track3r-os writer refuses exFAT volumes and cards with a write-protected CSD, and it never creates the `Firmware/` folder: it must already exist.
4. **Settings.** The vendor tells users to create a new project after an update so that Config is initialised (the vendor's statement, not verified here). Config may start from defaults after a change of firmware in either direction. How the settings of track3r-os and the official firmware interact needs more testing.
5. **Image end (v1.2.0).** An image must end at or below 0xFF000: an image that reached the last 4 KiB flash sector (end 0x100000) hung a unit after the update, which handed over to the bootloader and did not come back. The update checker of the unit and the image check of the build now refuse such an image, and the v1.2.0, v1.3.0 and v1.3.1 `.ptf` files end below the limit. If you build your own image, build it as a release build.
6. **Power.** Use a stable USB power source and do not remove power or the card while the unit is updating. This is a precaution; how long the flashing takes and what the screen shows while it runs has not been recorded.

## 1. From the official firmware

What is established:

- The bootloader flashes a `.ptf` (Intel HEX) from `Firmware/` on the card. It does flash a file whose name does not start with `PolyendTracker_` (observed on the unit, 2026-10-12, with a track3r-os test build started from the running track3r-os; `platform/mk66/README.md`, "Firmware update over USB").
- The official firmware's update menu has a file-name filter. Official 1.9.0 lists only names starting with `PolyendTracker` (observed on the unit; the filter of other versions is not known). **A track3r-os file named `track3r-os-<version>.ptf` is therefore not shown in the official update menu.** The release file is deliberately named differently, so that it cannot be mistaken for an official file. For the first install the copy on the card is renamed to start with `PolyendTracker` (see the steps below). The name changes two things. The official update menu lists the file. And track3r-os treats every name starting with `PolyendTracker` as official, so `fw rm` does not remove it: delete it from the computer if you want it gone.
- The hidden reset button flashes the **first** `.ptf` in `Firmware/` in directory order. This is how the maintainer's unit was recovered from every hung test image. The images it flashed there were named `PolyendTracker_0.0.x.ptf` (24 characters).
- The Polyend Tool app is **not supported** for this. It accepts only official files and answered "invalid firmware" to a track3r-os file. Two units were reported stuck on the "emergency update" screen with the file `track3r-os-v1.0.0.ptf`. Install straight from the SD card, as below.
- Users' reports (2026-10-25): the release file renamed to `PolyendTracker_0.0.1.ptf` installed from the card on a unit that ran the official firmware, after the same file under its release name had stuck on the "emergency update" screen. Another user reported that with the renamed file the reset button is not needed: the official firmware's own update menu installs it.

The steps this leaves:

1. Back up the card (above).
2. Copy `track3r-os-<version>.ptf` into the `Firmware/` folder of the card, and rename the copy to `PolyendTracker_0.0.1.ptf`. The new name must start with `PolyendTracker` and be at most 24 characters; `PolyendTracker_0.0.1.ptf` is exactly 24. Do not change the content of the file. Do not use the Polyend Tool app.
3. Make it the **only** `.ptf` in `Firmware/`: move any other `.ptf` (including the official one) out to your computer. With several files the button picks the first in directory order, which you cannot easily predict.
4. Put the card in the unit and use the hidden reset button as the vendor's emergency-flashing page describes. The position of the button is not recorded in this repository. A unit running the official firmware also installs the renamed file from its own update menu, without the button.
5. When the unit has restarted, open Config, INFO and check that BUILD ID shows the version you installed (the file name does not say what is installed; BUILD ID does). If the display looks corrupted on the first boot, power-cycle the unit: this was seen once after the bootloader flashed an early test image and a power cycle fixed it.

If the file does not flash, nothing is changed on the unit; say so in an issue with the file name you used and your model.

Later updates from a running track3r-os (section 2, or Config, INFO, `F8`) keep the plain `track3r-os-<version>.ptf` name.

## 2. Updating track3r-os to a newer track3r-os

An image of track3r-os has the `diag` console on its USB serial port and can write a new image to the card and ask the bootloader to flash it (OS-006c, `docs/specs/OS-006-usb.md`). The tool is `platform/mk66/tools/o3console.py` (Python 3, standard library only; it needs `check_image.py` from the same folder, so use a checkout of this repository). It checks the file locally and refuses a file that fails.

1. Back up the card. Connect the unit by USB (it enumerates as `16d0:0e9f`, the same USB ID as the official Tracker; the product name is "Track3r", the maker "track3r-os").
2. Any SD card in the unit takes the file. To make the tool check the card, find its volume serial (the `fw` command of the `diag` console prints it as `XXXX-XXXX`, a FAT volume ID) and pass it with `--expect-volume XXXX-XXXX`; the tool then refuses to write to a different card.
3. Send the file. The name must match `[0-9A-Za-z][0-9A-Za-z._-]{0,25}.ptf` and has at most 30 characters with `.ptf` (with a longer name the SD bootloader was seen flashing the first `.ptf` of `Firmware/` instead of the file you named, so the tool and the unit refuse it):

   ```sh
   python3 -I platform/mk66/tools/o3console.py --put track3r-os-v0.5.1.ptf --name track3r-os-v0.5.1.ptf
   ```

   The unit validates the stream while it writes, reads the file back from the card and checks it again, and answers `ok <name> <bytes> <crc> image <length>`. It never leaves a half-written `.ptf`. An image must end on a 4 KiB boundary (the build pads it): the SD bootloader leaves a short last sector as it was, so an image that does not (v1.0.0 is one) may crash at boot, and the tool, the unit's `fw` command and `fw put` refuse it (**IMAGE NOT PADDED: MAY NOT BOOT**). The Update screen on the unit does not refuse such an image: it says it is not padded and asks whether track3r-os may pad a copy (**PAD**); after you confirm, it writes `pad-<name>.ptf` next to the file (zeros up to the next 4 KiB boundary, the file you chose stays as it is), checks the copy, and asks again before it installs the copy. If that name is already taken, nothing is written and the copy that is there is kept: pick it from the list. Any other fault still refuses. From a computer, `o3console.py --put FILE --pad` makes the same copy, and `--update NAME --crc <crc> --yes-update --pad` asks the unit to pad (`fw arm NAME <crc> pad`); the reset button and the official update menu work as before. New Community OS behaviour.
4. Update. This restarts the unit into the bootloader, so the tool asks for `--yes-update`. `<crc>` is the CRC-32 from the release notes (the `ok` line of the put prints the same value):

   ```sh
   python3 -I platform/mk66/tools/o3console.py --update track3r-os-v0.5.1.ptf --crc <crc> --yes-update --expect-version v0.5.1
   ```

   The tool waits for the unit to come back, runs `version`, and fails if the version does not contain the text you expect. If the bootloader does not take over within 5 seconds the unit reports `ERR bootloader did not take over` and the update is cancelled.
5. Afterwards `Firmware/` holds every `.ptf` you put there. Remember the reset-button rule: it flashes the first one. `fw` marks that file with `*`. Remove the files you do not want (`fw rm <name>`; it keeps the last `.ptf`, and never removes a name starting with `Polyend`), or move them off the card on your computer.

What has been seen: the update path flashed a track3r-os test build on the maintainer's unit and the unit came back as that build (2026-10-12). More testing is needed for the whole sequence above with a release file, and for several of the checklist items in `platform/mk66/README.md` (FW-3 to FW-10, for example a card with its write-protect tab set, a pulled cable during the upload, the fallback after five seconds).

The alternative is the card route of section 1: put the new file alone in `Firmware/` and use the reset button.

A unit that already runs a track3r-os with the update dialog can also install a `.ptf` that is on its card from the unit itself, with no computer: see [Update from the unit](config.md#update-from-the-unit) in the Config chapter.

## Going back to the official firmware

The bootloader is separate from the application, so a broken or unwanted application does not remove the recovery path. The way back that has been proven on the unit is the hidden reset button with a single good `.ptf` in `Firmware/`.

**Going back from v1.3.1, v1.3.0, v1.2.0 or v1.1.0 to v1.0.1 or v1.0.0** works through the on-device Update screen too. Those files are not padded to a 4 KiB sector, so the screen offers to pad a copy first (**PAD**), then installs the copy (see [Update](config.md)). The reset button as below, with the older file alone in `Firmware/`, works as well.

**Projects when you go back from v1.3.0 to v1.2.0.** A project with MIDI lanes has an `MEVT` chunk, which v1.2.0 keeps as an unknown chunk and does not play. An instrument with CC letters is saved as INST 1.9; v1.2.0 says "newer fields skipped" and opens the rest.

**Instrument files when you go back to v1.1.0.** A project that uses wavetable envelopes, Play Thru or a module RATE is saved with a newer instrument version (INST 1.6, 1.7 or 1.8). It opens in v1.1.0, but v1.1.0 loses those values on its next save. A project that uses none of them is written byte for byte as before, and projects saved by v1.1.0 open in v1.2.0. Keep a copy of such a project before you open it in an older version. Going back to the official firmware is a different step: see below. New Community OS behaviour.

1. Put the card on your computer. Move **every** `.ptf` out of `Firmware/` (the track3r-os files and any other).
2. Copy the official `PolyendTracker_<version>.ptf` you kept (or downloaded from Polyend) into `Firmware/`, so that it is the only `.ptf` there.
3. Put the card in the unit and use the hidden reset button as in the vendor's emergency-flashing page.
4. When the official firmware is running, create a new project if its Config looks reset, as the vendor advises after an update.

track3r-os has its own update screen on the device (Config, INFO, `F8`; see [Update from the unit](config.md#update-from-the-unit)). It lists every `.ptf` in `Firmware/`, so the official `PolyendTracker_<version>.ptf` can be chosen there, and the card can hold several files. On the unit this screen has reached **IMAGE OK**. As a way back with an official file it needs more testing, and so does the official firmware's own update menu, which will also list an official file named `PolyendTracker...`, when track3r-os is the starting point. Use the reset button above when you need the way back to be certain.

Open research question: whether the official firmware opens projects saved by track3r-os (it reads the original formats; the native track3r-os project format is its own), and what happens to the unit's stored settings when you switch back. Keep your original-firmware projects as they are and work on copies.

## If something goes wrong

- The unit does not start after an update: do the steps of [Going back](#going-back-to-the-official-firmware). It is the same recovery used for every hung test image.
- The reset button flashed a file you did not expect: there was more than one `.ptf` in `Firmware/`. Leave exactly one.
- The unit sits on the "emergency update" screen and does not flash: check that the file on the card is named `PolyendTracker_0.0.1.ptf` (not `track3r-os-<version>.ptf`) and that it is the only `.ptf` in `Firmware/`. Do not use the Polyend Tool app.
- The pads do not answer after the install, while the buttons and the screen work: this happened with v1.0.0 on later units (plastic back; issue #1) and is fixed in v1.0.1, which a user with such a unit confirmed (2026-10-26). If your unit runs v1.0.0, install the current release (v1.2.0) the same way. If the pads still do not answer on v1.2.0, report it (OS-BUG-PADS). Open the [Input test](input_test.md) screen (hold `Shift`, `F1` and `F8` while you switch on) and press some pads. The board's status LED (a user saw it blinking behind the buttons under the screen) gives one short blink a second while track3r-os runs; 13 quick flashes after power-on, before that blink starts, mean a key scanner did not answer at boot. Report both in an issue with your model, and go back to the official firmware if you need the pads ([Going back](#going-back-to-the-official-firmware)).
- The unit is not found by `o3console.py`: check the USB cable, and that the unit runs track3r-os (the `diag` console is part of track3r-os).
- Report problems with the version string from Config, INFO (or the `version` command) and the file name and SHA-256 you installed.

## Open items (summary)

| Item | Status |
|---|---|
| The release file renamed to `PolyendTracker_0.0.1.ptf` installs on a unit that runs the official firmware | works (users' reports, 2026-10-25) |
| The official firmware's update menu installs the renamed file, without the reset button | works (a user's report, 2026-10-25) |
| The pads on every board revision | v1.0.0 left the pads dead on a later unit (plastic back, 2026-10-25, OS-BUG-PADS); v1.0.1 works there (one user, 2026-10-26); other revisions not reported |
| Position of the hidden reset button | not recorded here; see the vendor page |
| Time the flashing takes and what the screen shows | not recorded |
| Full USB update sequence with a release file, and checklist FW-3 to FW-10 | more testing needed |
| The update screen of track3r-os (Config, INFO, `F8`) installing the official file | IMAGE OK reached with a track3r-os file; more testing needed with an official file |
| Official firmware's update menu as a way back from track3r-os | more testing needed |
| Settings and project compatibility between track3r-os and the official firmware | open research question |

# Getting started

Status: draft

track3r-os runs in place of the official firmware on the same unit and the same card, and the way back to the official firmware stays open. Read this chapter once before you install anything: it says what goes on the card, what the first start looks like and how to return. The install steps themselves are in [Installing track3r-os](install.md). For your first sound, go to [Quick start](quick_start.md).

## What it is for

track3r-os is an operating system for the Polyend Tracker. The community wrote it. It is unofficial and not affiliated with or endorsed by Polyend. It runs in place of the official firmware on your unit. Read this chapter once before you install anything.

> **Careful**: track3r-os is unofficial community firmware. Back up the whole SD card before you install anything. Copy everything on it to your computer: projects, samples, modules and the `Firmware/` folder.

## Before you start

You need:

- a Tracker, with a USB cable;
- an SD card with one FAT32 partition. track3r-os refuses exFAT cards;
- a computer, to copy files and to download the release.

Keep a copy of the official firmware file on your computer, named `PolyendTracker_<version>.ptf`. You need it to go back. The vendor pages are linked from [Installing track3r-os](install.md).

## What goes on the card

The card holds your projects and the files the unit reads at start-up.

| Folder or file | What it holds |
|---|---|
| `Firmware/` | the firmware file, `.ptf`. The folder must already exist. track3r-os does not create it. |
| `Workspace/` | the project the unit loads at boot when no recently opened project is on the card, if the folder holds `project.mt`. The project is in the original firmware format. |
| `Projects/` | the projects you save, one folder for each. |
| `modules/` | the `.tmod` files: instrument and effect modules, file importers and apps. Apps go in `modules/apps/`. |

A starter zip is not part of this release. If you have one, you unpack it into the root of the card. It is meant to hold these folders and files:

| In the zip | What it holds |
|---|---|
| `Firmware/` | the update file and its checksum |
| `modules/apps/` | apps for the TOOLS screen. The TB-303, chip, FM and SID instruments are `.tmod` files in `modules/instruments/` (their factory presets are in the modules; your own are in `modules/presets/`). The apps alone come in `track3r-os-<version>-apps.zip`, in the release `apps-v<version>`. |
| `modules/effects/` | the effect modules for a track's insert |
| `modules/instruments/` | the instrument modules: TB-303, Chip, FM, SID and Sine. They are not inside the firmware (it keeps the flash free): a project that uses one without its file shows it greyed, **MODULE NOT ON THE CARD**. |
| `modules/importers/` | the importer module `tracker.tmod`, which the firmware loads from the card to read MOD, S3M and OctaMED files on IMPORT (File screen, F6). Without it an import says **NO IMPORTER** and changes nothing. |
| `Effects/` | the Sample Editor plugins (`.ptfx`): Add Silence, Analog Kick, Chiptune, Multimode Filter, Stereo Delay, Stereo to Mono, Overdrive, Delay, Bitcrusher, Chorus, Flanger, Limiter, Three-Band EQ, and six of our own: WT Forge, WT Notes, Grain Lock, Pad Forge, WT Resynth and Pad Stretch |
| `Samples/` | a drum kit and other one-shots |
| `WTABLE/` | wavetables |
| `Songs/` | tracker songs for the importers |
| `Projects/` | two demo projects |
| `LICENSES/` | the licence texts and the credits |
| `README.txt` | what goes where |
| `SHA256SUMS` | the checksum of every file |

## More tasks

### Install track3r-os

Follow [Installing track3r-os](install.md). It has the update steps, the checks and what to do when the unit does not start. This chapter does not repeat them.

1. Download the release from the project's Releases page on GitHub. It has two files: `track3r-os-<version>.ptf` and `SHA256SUMS`. The starter zip described above is not part of the release. The apps are a separate download: the release `apps-v<version>` on the Releases page holds `track3r-os-<version>-apps.zip`. Unpack it into the root of the card.
2. Check the download with `sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS`.
3. Back up the card, then follow the steps in [Installing track3r-os](install.md).

### Check the version

Use this after an install, to confirm which build the unit runs.

1. Press `Config`.
2. Open the INFO page.
3. Look at **BUILD ID**. It shows the version and a short build code, for example `v0.5.0 (0271ab60bea6)`.

You should see the version you installed. The boot screen shows the same version.

### Start the unit for the first time

1. Turn the unit on.
2. The boot screen shows a logo with **Track3r** and the build under it. It stays for at least 0.8 s, until the start-up work is done.
3. The unit opens the project you had open last (the newest of the File screen's RECENT list) if it is still on the card. With none, and a `Workspace/project.mt` file on the card, it loads that. When the last project cannot be read (a damaged file, a project from a newer OS), the unit starts empty and the strip says `PROJECT <name> FAILED` and why; it does not fall back to the Workspace, and it tries the same project on every start until you open another one in File. The strip shows the end of the load: `PROJECT <name> OPENED`. The inserts saved with the project are bound again as it loads.
4. If no project loads, or the loaded project has no sample or module instrument and no instrument at all in slots 1 to 48 (MIDI instruments in slots 49 to 64, the 16 MIDI channels of every project from the official firmware, do not stop it), the unit starts the demo kit: four instruments and pattern 1. This is new Community OS behaviour, a default the maintainer still has to confirm. Press `Play` to start pattern 1.

To open another project from the card, press `File`. See [File](file.md). For where each key is, see [The panel](panel.md). On any screen, hold `Shift` and tap `Config` to read a help page for it ([the help page](panel.md#the-help-page)).

### Turn the unit off

`Power` is the small button on the rear panel. Save your work first: press `F4` (**SAVE**) on the File screen. The off does not save for you.

(Picture: Panel: the Power button on the rear panel is ringed. Hold it for 2 seconds.)

1. Hold `Power`. A line across the top of the screen fills over 2 seconds.
2. Keep holding until the line is full. The strip says **POWERING OFF**. The keys and pads stop working, the screen fades, the pad lights go out and the sound stops.
3. Let go of `Power`. The unit stays dark. Press `Power` and let go to start it again.

To cancel, let go before the line is full, or press `Shift` while you hold `Power`.  `Shift` + `Power` on its own is not an off: it saves a screenshot to the card ([The panel](panel.md#screenshot)).  To remove all power, unplug the USB cable. For saves and exports during the off, see [The panel](panel.md#power). **Known gap:** a click may be heard at power off and at power on.

### Use the card on a computer

In this mode the unit shows its card to the computer as a disk. The unit does not load a project and does not open its audio outputs. Start with the unit off and connected to the computer with USB.

1. Hold `Shift`, `F1` and `F7` together, and turn the unit on (the keys are on the figure in [The panel](panel.md#keys-held-when-the-unit-turns-on)). Keep them held until the strip says **USB DISK - EJECT ON THE COMPUTER OR PRESS A KEY**.
2. Let the keys go. The computer lists the card as one writable disk.
3. You can unmount and mount the card on the computer without ejecting it. The card comes back with the same files.
4. When you are done, eject the disk on the computer. Then press a key on the unit. If the computer has not ejected the disk, press a key twice within 5 seconds: the first only warns.

The strip says **DISK EJECTED - PRESS ANY KEY TO RESTART**, and the unit restarts with the card in place.  For the details, and for sharing the card while the unit plays, see [USB disk](usb_disk.md).

### Go back to the official firmware

Follow [Going back to the official firmware](install.md#going-back-to-the-official-firmware). It has the steps and the checks.

Keep your projects from the original firmware as they are. Work on copies in track3r-os.

## Good to know

- Projects saved by the original firmware open in track3r-os. This is tested on the host with files made from the format's byte maps.
- Projects saved in track3r-os may not open on the official firmware. Open research question.
- The unit's settings may start from defaults after a change of firmware, in either direction. Open research question. Keep copies of your projects.

## See also

- [Installing track3r-os](install.md): the update steps, the checks and the way back.
- [The panel](panel.md): where each key is and what it does.
- [File](file.md): projects, saving and loading.
- [USB disk](usb_disk.md): the card on a computer.
- [Computer tools](computer_tools.md): the USB tools for a computer.

# The panel

Status: draft

The panel page is the map of the unit: where each key is and what it does on every screen. Two things are worth knowing before you read on. `Shift` relabels the soft keys `F1` to `F8`, and the unit draws that second row while you hold it. The keys you hold while the unit turns on choose a start mode, such as the USB disk. Not checked against the original firmware: the key layout.

## What it is for

Use this page to find a key on the unit and to see what it does. Read it when a chapter says "press `Shift` + `F3`" and you do not know where the key is.

(Picture: Panel of the unit: screen, eight soft keys and pad grid on the left; screen buttons, edit block and encoder on the right.)

*The drawing is schematic and not to scale.*

## The parts

The screen is at the top left. Under it are eight soft keys, `F1` to `F8`. Each soft key runs the label printed on the screen above it, so the labels change from one screen to the next. Under the soft keys is a grid of 48 pads: 12 columns and 4 rows.

The block at the top right holds the screen buttons. Each one opens a screen, and pressing it again opens the next page of that screen. Below that block is the edit and transport block, and at the bottom right is the encoder.

Holding `Shift` changes what the other keys do. `Shift` relabels `F1` to `F8`: while it is held, the key row shows the second labels of the screen. `Shift` + a soft key runs that label. In this manual, `Shift` + `F3` means: hold `Shift`, press `F3`, then release both.

## Keys on the screen (F1 to F8)

Each soft key does what its label says on the screen in view. These are examples from two screens.

| Key | On Pattern | On Mixer | Ref |
|---|---|---|---|
| `F1` | opens the PATTERN chooser (a tap keeps it open, a hold shows it while held) | shows the MIXER page | - |
| `F2` | opens the LENGTH chooser | shows the ROUTING page | - |
| `F3` | opens the JUMP chooser | shows the MST FX page | - |
| `F4` | **FILL**: opens the Fill dialog | shows the STEMS page | QA-PAT-086 |
| `F5` | **PREVIEW** | **CUE LVL**: goes to the cue level | - |
| `F6` | **EVENTS** (the event list; **RE FILL** / **REPEAT**, the last fill or TOOLS apply again, is `F6` of the `F7` verb menu) | - | QA-PAT-435, QA-PAT-470 |
| `F7` | **TOOLS**: opens the verb menu (pads 1-16 pick a verb); held + a pad runs the verb directly | **MUTE**: mutes the track under the cursor | QA-PAT-436, QA-PAT-456 |
| `F8` | **UNDO** (`Shift` + `F8` is **REDO**) | **SOLO**: solos the track under the cursor | QA-PAT-089 |

If a `Shift` + soft key has no label, it does nothing. It never acts as the plain key.

## Screen buttons

(Picture: Screen map: the eleven screen buttons with the screen each opens, and how to reach Modules, the Input test and an app page.)

| Key | Opens | Ref |
|---|---|---|
| `Instrument Parameters` (`Params`) | the Instrument screen | - |
| `Perform` | the Perform screen | - |
| `File` | the File screen | - |
| `Config` | the Config screen | - |
| `Master` | the Mixer, when you let go of the key. Held, with the encoder: the master volume, on any screen ([Mixer](mixer.md)) | - |
| `Sample Loader` | the Sample load screen | - |
| `Sample Playback` | the Wave and Chop screen | - |
| `Sample Editor` | the Sample edit screen | - |
| `Sample Recorder` | the Record screen | - |
| `Song` | the Song screen, when you let go of the key. Held: the Song screen until you let go, then back to where you were ([Song](song.md)) | - |
| `Pattern` | the Pattern screen, when you let go of the key. Held, with the encoder: the tempo, on any screen; held, with a pad: tap tempo (see [Tempo from any screen](#tempo-from-any-screen)) | QA-GLB-153, QA-GLB-155 |
| `Song` + `Pattern`, or `Master` + `Song`, pressed together | opens the Navigator on any screen; press `F1` (**GO**) to go to the screen you chose, or `F8` (**BACK**) to leave it. Neither key does its own job, and the Song peek and the held volume and tempo turns stay off | QA-GLB-233 |
| `Master` + `Insert`, pressed together | opens the Mixer on its **INSERTS** page from any screen (on the Mixer it goes to INSERTS). Neither key does its own job. New in track3r-os. | QA-MIX-112 |
| `Master` held, then `Insert` at any later time | the same: hold `Master`, take your time, tap `Insert`; letting go of `Master` afterwards does nothing. (`Insert` first and `Master` later is not this: `Insert` acts on its own.) Any other key pressed that way (`Play`, say) does its own job and `Master`'s release is silent; earlier builds opened the Mixer on that key. New in track3r-os. Checked on the unit. | QA-MIX-112 |
| `Shift` + `Pattern` | lists the module apps that are not tools; `F1` (**LAUNCH**) starts one, `Pattern` leaves the list. It was the Navigator before | QA-MOD-252 |
| `Shift` + `Master` | steps to the next colour theme: Amiga, Black, White, then Amiga again. The THEME row on Config says the same. New in track3r-os. | QA-GLB-157 |
| `Shift` + `Config` | opens the help page of the screen you are on (see [The help page](#the-help-page)) | QA-GLB-141 |

(Picture: Panel: Song and Pattern are marked. Press both together to open the Navigator.)

## Tempo from any screen

New in track3r-os. Hold `Pattern` on any screen and the encoder and the pads set the tempo. The screen does not change.

- **Turn the encoder** while you hold `Pattern`: the tempo moves 1 BPM a detent, between 40 and 800 BPM. Hold `Shift` first, then `Pattern`, and a detent is a tenth of a BPM. The sequencer follows at once, also while it plays, and the strip says, for example, **TEMPO 137.0 BPM**.
- **Tap pads** while you hold `Pattern`, about half a second apart. The first tap says **TAP**. From the second, the tempo is the mean of the last four gaps, to a tenth of a BPM, between 40 and 300 BPM, and the strip says, for example, **TAP 120.0 BPM**. A pause of more than 2 seconds starts a new series. The pad plays no note. With `Pattern` up, a pad is a pad again.

The turns and taps of one hold are one undo step on the screen in view: one `Undo` brings back the tempo from before the hold. Letting go of `Pattern` after a turn or a tap opens nothing. `Shift` pressed after `Pattern` ends the gesture, and the turn is the screen's own.

Nothing happens in a dialog or the Navigator, on a module app's page, or when CLOCK MODE is **Slave**: there the strip says **MIDI SLAVE: THE CLOCK SETS THE TEMPO**. `Master` + the encoder is unchanged.

A tap of `Pattern` with no turn or pad acts when you let go of the key, and so does `Shift` + `Pattern`, because `Pattern` now waits for a turn or a pad. A long hold with no turn is still a tap. Inside the Navigator, `Pattern` closes it at the press as before.

## The help page

New in track3r-os. Hold `Shift` and tap `Config` on any screen to read about it without leaving it.

1. Hold `Shift` and tap `Config`. A page titled **HELP: SONG** (for the Song screen) opens over the screen, with a page count such as **3/15** at the right of its bar. The key row reads **CLOSE** on `F8` and is blank otherwise.
2. Press `Left` or `Right` to turn the pages. They stop at **1/15**, the Global page (the screen buttons and the global keys), and at **15/15**.
3. Press `Up` or `Down`, or turn the encoder, to scroll one line. With `Shift` held they scroll a screenful. `Shift` alone neither scrolls nor closes.
4. Press any other key to close it.

Every screen has a page of its own, with a paragraph, **KEYS** and **PADS**. Perform has two: **HELP: PERFORM** (10/15) and **HELP: PERFORM DJ** (11/15), and the page that opens is the one for the Perform page you are on.

- The key that closes help does nothing else: `Play` does not start the transport, a screen button does not change the screen, and an `F` key posts no label. A pad closes it and plays no note.
- A pad you hold when help opens still ends its note when you let go. That let-go does not close help.
- Each page keeps its scroll. `Shift` + `Config` opens the page at the scroll you left it. The scrolls are kept in memory only, so every page starts at the top after a power cycle.
- Under a dialog (Learn, the Navigator, a chooser, the on-screen keyboard) `Shift` + `Config` does nothing. Close the dialog first.
- On a module app's page, help opens over the app. The app hears nothing while the page is up, and takes input again after it closes.

## Column and colour keys

These four keys select a column of the Pattern grid. They work on the Pattern screen.

| Key | Colour | What it does on Pattern | Ref |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Note` | teal | selects the Note column; hold it to open the note popup | - |
| `Instr` | yellow | selects the Instr column; hold it to open the instrument list. The tap acts when you let go of the key, so `Instr` with `Vol` or `Fx` is a chord and selects nothing | - |
| `Vol` | purple | selects the volume column. The step grid calls this column **VOL**. Hold the key to open its popup. The tap acts when you let go of the key. | - |
| `Fx` | cyan | selects the FX column; hold `Fx` and turn the encoder to change the FX type | - |

### Learn a MIDI control

Press `Vol` and `Fx` together to open Learn.

(Picture: Panel: Vol and Fx are marked. Press both together to open Learn.)

The Learn dialog works on the row under the cursor of the screen below. Move a MIDI control (a CC) and it binds to that row: the target line names the parameter, its instrument and the controller (`CC 74 PICKUP`). `F1` unbinds it, `F2` changes how the controller moves it (**MODE**: pickup, jump, relative), `F3` deletes the binding the list's cursor is on, `F4` clears them all (pressed twice), `F7` **ENC** puts the row on the encoder (see [Put one parameter on the encoder](#put-one-parameter-on-the-encoder)), `F8` goes back. `F5` **FOLLOW** makes the binding follow the selected instrument instead of its own — the target line then reads `INS *` and the binding text ends `FOLLOW` — and `F5` again pins it back to its instrument. The key row names `F5` only when the target is an instrument parameter with a binding.

Use your keyboard as a synth: bind the knobs on one instrument, press `F5` on each, then select any instrument — the same knobs now shape whichever instrument is selected. A binding follows instrument parameters only, and it acts only when the selected instrument has the row with its meaning (a sampler row on a MIDI instrument does nothing). A follow binding is saved with the project.

### See every binding: LEARN MAP

LEARN MAP is one full-screen list of every binding of both stores, with the encoder's target on the first row (`ENC`). Open it with `F6` (**MAP**) in the Learn dialog, or with `F8` (**MAP**) on the Config MIDI page. Each row shows the **SOURCE** (the CC), its **CH** (`*` is every channel), the **PARAMETER**, the **INS** (an instrument number, or `*` for a binding that follows the selected instrument), the **MODE**, and the live **VALUE**. A dot at the left of a row lights while its CC moves and goes out a quarter of a second later.

`Up` and `Down` move the row, `Left` and `Right` pick the column, and the encoder changes it (`Shift` and the encoder: coarse steps; `Shift` + `Up` / `Down`: a page of rows). PARAMETER walks only the parameters the instrument has (a sampler's list for a sampler, the MIDI rows for a MIDI instrument). An INS that has no such parameter is refused: `INS 05 HAS NO CUTOFF`. A CC that another binding already uses on that channel is refused: `CC 74 CH1 IS TAKEN`. A refusal changes nothing. Each edit is one undo step, as in the Learn dialog (close the map with `F8`, then undo).

`F1` **NEW**: move a knob and the next CC becomes a new binding on the selected instrument. `F2` **MODE** steps pickup, jump and relative. `F3` **DELETE** removes the row (on the `ENC` row it clears the encoder's target). `F4` **CLR ALL**, pressed twice, removes every binding. `F5` **FOLLOW** switches a row between its instrument and the selected one. `F7` **RELEARN**: the next CC you move becomes the row's source. `F8` goes back. The `ENC` row takes no CC, mode or follow. Nothing here changes a file: the project's bindings are saved with the project as before, and the encoder's target is not saved.

New in track3r-os.

### Put one parameter on the encoder

The encoder can work like a MIDI knob that you bound with Learn, with no MIDI controller. You pick a parameter once. Then you hold two keys and turn the encoder to move it, on any screen. It is a relative control: it has no CC number to set and no pickup, and every click moves the value one step.

Any row that Learn can bind can also sit on the encoder, without a MIDI controller. Put the cursor on the row (for example on the Instrument screen), press `Vol` and `Fx` together to open Learn, then press `F7` (**ENC**). The dialog closes and the strip says `ENCODER: <PARAM> INS <n>`. A row Learn cannot bind says `NO TARGET FOR ENCODER` and the encoder keeps its old target. There is one encoder target in all: `F7` on another row replaces it, and `F7` on the same row again only shows the message again. The old chord `Instr` and `Fx` does nothing now. There is no clear gesture. The target stays on that row and that instrument until you replace it or switch the unit off. It is not saved.

To use it, hold `Instr` and `Vol` and turn the encoder, on any screen with no dialog open. Each click moves the row by one step; hold `Shift` for the coarse step. The strip shows `<PARAM> <value>`. Moves undo like a Learn knob. With no target the strip says `NO ENCODER TARGET (SET IT IN LEARN)`. While both keys are held the encoder does nothing else. Turning cancels the `Instr` popup and the `Vol` tap, so a turn never selects a column. Pressing the two keys without turning does nothing.

Recording follows the Learn rule, and a row with no FX of its own now records too. In LIVE recording, with Record knob moves as FX on, a move writes the matching FX on the playing step (cutoff, panning, delay send, reverb send, overdrive and bit depth have one). In Edit with free recording, a move writes the FX on the cursor's step of the cursor's track, and one hold of the two keys is one undo unit. Browse records nothing.

Any other parameter of a Sample or Module instrument is recorded as a CC letter, **CC A** to **CC F**, in the step's FX column. The first recorded move takes the first free letter of the project, and the strip says `REC FX: VOLUME -> CC A`. Turning the same row again reuses its letter; the next row takes the next one (TUNE takes **CC B**). There are six letters, so a seventh parameter says `REC FX: NO FREE CC LETTER`: the move still sounds and nothing is written. On a track whose instrument is a MIDI one the strip says `REC FX: MIDI TRACK` and nothing is written, because a letter there would send a MIDI CC. Rows that cannot take a letter (VEL>, Track, Master, Insert) still say `REC FX: <PARAM> HAS NO FX` on the first move of a hold.

One Undo takes the step and its letter back together, and leaves the other parameters you changed since as they are. On playback a mapped letter moves the parameter on its own instrument; it sends no MIDI. An older `CC x` step of a non-MIDI track in the same project now does the same. Playing such a step does not change the project: it stays saved, a save during playback works, and when playback stops the parameter returns to the value saved in the project. An export does not render these moves and says **CC LETTER MOVES NOT RENDERED**.

The encoder target differs from a Learn binding in four ways. It is not listed in Learn and it is not saved with the project: it is gone when you switch the unit off. It is one parameter, not a list. It stays on the instrument you picked, so it does not follow the selected instrument as a Learn binding does with `F5` (**FOLLOW**).

Try it. Start on the Instrument screen.

1. Press `F3` (**FILTER**) and put the cursor on CUTOFF.
2. Press `Vol` and `Fx` together, then `F7` (**ENC**). The strip says **ENCODER: CUTOFF INS 1**, with your instrument's number.
3. Press `Pattern` to leave the screen. Press `Play` so a sound is playing.
4. Hold `Instr` and `Vol` and turn the encoder. The strip says **CUTOFF** and its value, and you hear the filter move.
5. Let go of both keys. The encoder does its usual job again, and the target stays set.

New in track3r-os.

## Edit block

Each key has a second label printed on it. `Shift` + the key runs that label.

| Key | Plain behaviour on Pattern | `Shift` + key | Ref |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Copy` (second label: Paste) | copies the selected block, or the step under the cursor; with `F1` held, the whole pattern | `Shift` + `Copy` pastes the clipboard at the cursor; with `F1` held, it writes a whole-pattern copy over the pattern shown | - |
| `Insert` (second label: Home) | inserts an empty step at the cursor and pushes the steps below it down. With a block selected, it works from the block's first step, on every track of the block | `Shift` + `Insert` goes to step 0 and clears the block selection | - |
| `Delete` (second label: Backspace) | clears what the cursor column holds: the whole step in Note or Instr, the volume in Vol, the FX in Fx. With a block selected, it clears the highlighted columns, or whole steps when the block spans tracks. | `Shift` + `Delete` removes the step under the cursor and pulls the steps below up, to close a gap. It is the reverse of `Insert`, and works from the block's first step when a block is selected. | - |
| `Up`, `Down`, `Left`, `Right` | move the cursor | `Shift` + `Up` or `Down` selects the block; `Shift` + `Left` or `Right` grows a block of columns one column at a time; past the last column it takes the next track whole | QA-PAT-007, QA-PAT-319 |

A block can cover just some columns of one track. `Delete` and `Copy` then act on those columns only, while Fill and the TOOLS menu always take whole steps, and the strip says **WHOLE STEPS** when they do.  See [Pattern](pattern.md).

On the Song screen, `Insert` adds a slot, `Shift` + `Insert` adds a slot with a copy of the pattern, and `Delete` removes the slot, or clears the selected cells when the cursor is in the track map. `Shift` + `Delete` cuts instead: the slot (or the selected slots) goes into the slot clipboard and out of the list, and in the track map the selected cells go into the song clip and are cleared; `Shift` + `Copy` puts them back anywhere. Hold `Copy` and press `Up` or `Down` to move the slot (or the selected slots) one place, and keep the arrow held to go on. `Note` jumps to the next slot that holds the same pattern, and `Shift` + `Note` to the previous one. The cut, the move and the jump are new in track3r-os. On lists, `Shift` + `Up` and `Shift` + `Down` move one page.

The second label Backspace is not what `Shift` + `Delete` does on Pattern: it pulls steps up and erases nothing backwards. The backspace is the plain `Delete` key on the on-screen keyboard. The pull is new in track3r-os.

Most screen buttons act when you press them. `Pattern`, `Song`, `Master` and `Insert` act when you let go (or 40 ms after the press), because a hold can mean something else: `Song` + `Pattern` and `Master` + `Song` open the Navigator, `Master` + `Insert` opens the Mixer on INSERTS (press both within 40 ms of each other, or hold `Master` and tap `Insert` whenever you like; `Insert` first and `Master` later is `Insert`'s own key, then `Master`) and `Shift` + `Pattern` lists the module apps, and a hold of `Song` for 0.4 seconds shows the Song screen as a peek.  Playback does not stop when you change screen. Leaving Perform ends its effects, except when you go to the Mixer or Song; see [Perform](perform.md).

The buttons have no lights. The screen shows the state instead, for example the mode chip and the red **REC** badge on Pattern.

Some keys act on a tap and some only while you hold them. On Pattern, `F1` opens the pattern picker on a tap and while you hold it. On Pattern, `F7` held with a pad runs that verb without opening the menu, so a tap of `F7` opens the menu. On Pattern, `F1`, `F2` and `F3` toggle a chooser with a tap. On Song, `F7` selects the tempo field, and a second tap taps the tempo. On the Mixer, `F1` on the MIXER page changes nothing.

While a dialog or a list is open, it owns the key row: the row shows only the dialog's own keys, every other key is blank and does nothing, and `Shift` does not change the row. `F8` goes back. On the on-screen keyboard, `F1` keeps the text and `F8` cancels. Learn shows **BACK** on `F8` alone until it has a target or a binding, and **FOLLOW** on `F5` when the target is a bound instrument parameter (see "Learn a MIDI control" above). Fill shows **FILL** on `F1` and **BACK** on `F8`, and a running WAV export shows **CANCEL** on `F8`. The Navigator reads **GO** on `F1` and **BACK** on `F8`, and the same with `Shift` held. The screen buttons do nothing until the dialog closes. New in track3r-os. On Song, a question on the strip asks **ALL** (`F1`) or **UNIQUE** (`F2`), and any other key withdraws it. On Config, **APPLY** and **DEFAULTS** ask for a second press within a short time.

## Transport

| Key | Plain behaviour | `Shift` + key | Ref |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Play` | starts or stops the pattern you edit, from any screen | on Pattern, plays from the cursor's row | QA-PAT-126 |
| `Rec` | on Pattern, turns STEP editing on or off; on the Record screen, starts or stops the take | `Shift` + `Rec` turns LIVE recording on or off | QA-PAT-001 |

On Pattern, STEP lets you enter notes at the cursor while the pattern plays. LIVE records the notes you play at the play line.

## Pads

| Pads | What they do on Pattern | Ref |
|---|---|---|
| the 48 pads, mode NOTES (the default) | preview the sound in WATCH; write a note at the cursor in STEP | QA-PAT-006 |
| `Shift` + `F1` | the pads' octave: the lowest C of the pads goes up one octave, C9 goes back to C0. The key shows the octave, and the octave is saved with the project. New Community OS behaviour. | QA-PAT-313 |
| `Shift` + `F2` | PADS: open the list of pad modes. In the list `F1` NOTES, `F2` PIANO, `F3` ISO, `F4` TRACKS, `F5` PATS, `F6` VU, `F8` BACK | QA-PAT-314, QA-PAT-529 |
| `Shift` + `F8` | redoes | QA-PAT-314 |
| `Shift` held alone | the pads show the TRACKS layer while you hold it: each column is a track, with rows for track, mute, mute mode and solo. New Community OS behaviour. | - |

The pad mode stays until you change it and is not saved.

## Encoder

| Control | What it does | Ref |
|---|---|---|
| turn the encoder | changes the value under the cursor, or scrolls the list in view | - |
| `Shift` + turn the encoder | a coarse step on the Instrument screen; a fine step on the Song screen | - |
| turn the encoder quickly in a list | in File, Sample load, the Modules list and the module picker, a quick spin moves 4 rows a detent, then 8; a slow turn moves one. The Pattern cursor, every value and the `Shift` coarse steps are unchanged. New in track3r-os. The numbers are being tuned. | QA-GLB-159 |

With `Instr` and `Vol` both held, the encoder moves the parameter you picked with `F7` in Learn and does nothing else (see "Put one parameter on the encoder" above). New in track3r-os.

The encoder has no push function.

## Screenshot

`Shift` + `Power` saves what is on the screen to the card as a picture. New in track3r-os.

1. Put a card in the unit. Hold `Shift`, press `Power`, and let go of both.
2. The screen freezes for 1 to 2 seconds while the picture is written. The song plays on with no click or stutter.

You should see **SCREENSHOT SAVED: SHOT_0001.BMP** in the strip. The file is `Screenshots/SHOT_0001.bmp` on the card, 768,066 bytes. The next one is `SHOT_0002.bmp`, and no file is ever overwritten. A gap left by a deleted file is used only after 9999.

The picture shows the whole 800 x 480 screen as it is with no key held, so the key row has its plain labels, not the `Shift` labels.  Keys, pads and the encoder do nothing while the screen is frozen, and a pad you hold keeps its note until you let go.

The strip says why when it cannot save, and writes no file:

| The strip says | Why |
|---|---|
| **NO SCREENSHOT: NO CARD** | there is no card in the unit |
| **NO SCREENSHOT: CARD ON THE COMPUTER** | the computer has the card, as in [USB disk](usb_disk.md) |
| **NO SCREENSHOT: CARD BUSY** | an export or a save is running |
| **NO SCREENSHOT: CONSOLE SHOT RUNNING** | a picture is being taken from the computer |
| **SCREENSHOT FAILED** | the card was pulled during the write; no `SHOT_nnnn.bmp` is left |

`Power` held alone still turns the unit off, and `Shift` pressed during that hold cancels it with no screenshot.  To take the picture from a computer instead, see [Computer tools](computer_tools.md).

## Power

`Power` is the small button on the rear panel. Hold it for 2 seconds to turn the unit off. Step by step, see [Getting started](getting_started.md#turn-the-unit-off). New in track3r-os. The hold time, the off state and the wake are not checked against the original firmware.

| Key | What it does | Ref |
|---|---|---|
| `Power`, held | a line across the top fills over 2 seconds, and the strip says **HOLD TO SWITCH OFF**. The line is drawn over a dialog too. Let go before it is full, and the line empties. The unit stays on, and the music keeps playing. | QA-GLB-100 |
| `Power`, a tap under 150 ms | nothing | QA-GLB-101 |
| `Power`, let go from 150 ms to 2 seconds | the strip shows **HOLD POWER 2 S TO SWITCH OFF** for about 1.5 seconds | QA-GLB-101 |
| `Shift` + `Power` | a screenshot ([above](#screenshot)). No line, no hint and no off. | QA-GLB-110, QA-GLB-130 |
| `Power` held, then `Shift` | the line empties and the unit stays on. To turn it off, let go of `Power` and hold it again. | QA-GLB-110 |

When the line is full, the strip says **POWERING OFF**. The keys, the pads and the MIDI input stop working, the screen fades, the pad lights go out and the sound stops. If a song is playing, the unit sends note-offs and a MIDI Stop to the MIDI out, and the sound fades in about 50 ms. The unit is dark and silent, but it is not switched off at the power supply. To remove all power, unplug the USB cable.

If `Power` is still held when the line is full, the unit goes dark at once and stays dark after you let go.

**To start it again,** press `Power` and let go. The unit starts as after a power-up: the logo, then the project on the card. Nothing from before the off is kept, so work that was not saved is lost. Unplugging the USB cable and plugging it in again also starts the unit.

If `Power` is held when the unit starts, the hold does not count until you let go.

The off does not save for you. This is what happens to work in progress:

- **Unsaved work.** While the line fills, the strip says **UNSAVED WORK - LET GO TO KEEP IT** if the project has changes that are not saved, or if a recorded take or loop is not saved. Let go to keep working. After a save, the strip says **HOLD TO SWITCH OFF**. The off never saves for you, so a take or loop that is not saved is lost.
- **A save in progress.** The save gets up to 5 seconds to finish, and the strip says **SAVING... THEN POWER OFF**. A save that is still running after that is cancelled, and the strip says **SAVE CANCELLED - POWERING OFF**. The old project file stays whole. A Config change that is not written yet is written first.
- **An export.** The first hold is refused, and the strip says **EXPORT RUNNING - HOLD POWER AGAIN TO STOP IT**. The export goes on. A second full hold within 10 seconds stops the export and turns the unit off. The finished files stay. A stopped export to the original firmware format has no project file, so it does not load as a project. See [File](file.md).
- **A firmware update on the card.** Power is refused while the update runs, and the strip says **FIRMWARE UPDATE RUNNING**. The update is not touched.
- **A writable disk.** When the card is shown to the computer as a writable disk, the first hold only warns, and the strip says **COMPUTER MAY BE WRITING - HOLD AGAIN**. A second full hold within 10 seconds turns the unit off. If you eject the disk on the computer first, one hold turns the unit off at once. The unit cannot flush the computer's write cache. See [Getting started](getting_started.md#use-the-card-on-a-computer).

The two-second hold turns the unit off, and the screen goes dark and silent. A press of `Power` starts it again, and so does plugging the USB cable in again.

**Known gap:** a click may be heard at power off and at power on.

## Keys held when the unit turns on

The unit reads these keys when it starts. Hold them while you turn the unit on, until the strip shows the mode.

(Picture: Panel: Shift, F1, F7 (DISK) and F8 (TEST) are ringed. Hold Shift and F1 with F7 or F8 while you turn the unit on.)

| Keys held together | What happens | Ref |
|---|---|---|
| `Shift`, `F1` and `F7` | the card shows on the computer as a writable disk. See [Getting started](getting_started.md) | QA-GLB-015, QA-GLB-016 |
| `Shift` and `F1`; `Shift` and `F7`; `F1` and `F7` | the unit starts as normal | QA-GLB-016 |
| `Shift`, `F1` and `F8` | the **INPUT TEST** screen opens. `F7` held as well changes nothing | QA-GLB-015, QA-GLB-016 |
| `Shift`, `F1`, `F7` and `F8` | the **INPUT TEST** screen opens | QA-GLB-016 |

## See also

- [Mixer](mixer.md): the soft keys of the Mixer in detail.
- [Song](song.md): the slot keys and the order list.

# Song

Status: draft

Song is an editor, not only a list. Adding a slot with `F3` (**ADD SLOT**) works as before, and the new slot shares the pattern of the one you were on. New in track3r-os: a `*` marks slots that share a pattern, and `F5` (**UNIQUE**) gives a slot a copy of its own. `Right` steps from the list into a map of slots and tracks that you can copy, paste, clear and transpose, `F6` (**TOOLS**) opens the block tools, and the **TIMELINE** page is an editing grid with the same keys. The pads can pick slots, and holding `Song` shows the screen for a moment.

## What it is for

Use Song to arrange patterns in time. Press `Song`. The list holds the slots, and each slot holds one pattern number, the bar it starts at (**BAR**) and how many bars it lasts (**BARS**). The song plays the slots from the top. Press `Song` again for the **TIMELINE** page, which draws the song as blocks along the page. Two pages in all; the header says which one you are on (**LIST 1/2**, **TIMELINE 2/2**). The next press after **TIMELINE 2/2** goes back to **LIST 1/2**.

## How it works

### Slots and patterns

A pattern holds the notes. A slot is a place in the song that points at a pattern, like a playlist entry points at a track. Slots 1, 2, 1, 3 play verse, chorus, verse, bridge: pattern 1 is in the song twice.

- **Stored:** the order list is saved with the project.
- **Live:** `Play` plays the song from the selected slot. While it plays, a thin line under the **PAT** tile of the row that plays runs through the pattern with the playhead.  `F1` (**PLAY PAT**) loops only that slot's pattern. `F2` (**DUP PAT**) adds a slot after the cursor with a copy of its pattern, as `Shift` + `Insert` does; it replaces the old `F2` PLAY SNG, which `Play` already did (new Community OS behaviour).  At the end of the list the song goes round to the first slot. In a lane of the TIMELINE page `F1` (**PREVIEW**) instead loops that slot's pattern with only the selected tracks (the rectangle) sounding; `F1` again, `Stop` or leaving the screen restores the solo set as it was. New in the Community OS.   Not checked against the original firmware.
- **Jump:** while the song plays, `Rec` queues the cursor's slot. It starts after the pattern now playing, and the slot blinks until then. `Rec` on it again cancels.
- **Loop:** select the slots with `Shift` + `Up` / `Down` (the cursor's slot alone is enough) and hold `F2`. The song starts at the first of them, and after the last it goes back to the first. The info line says **LOOP 03-06**. Edit the patterns and the list meanwhile: a slot you delete inside the loop shortens it, a slot you add inside it lengthens it. `Rec` on a slot outside the loop leaves it, so does `Stop`; hold `F2` on the same slots again to leave it and keep playing. A tap of `F2` still plays the song, now at the release of the key. New Community OS behaviour.

### Sharing a pattern

`F3` (**ADD SLOT**) adds a slot with the same pattern number. Both slots now play one pattern, so a change made in Pattern is heard in both. Each sharing slot has a `*`, and the info line says, for example, **pattern 03 in 2 slots**. The other slots of the cursor's pattern also show their PAT number in a second ink.

Hold `Copy` and press `F3` (**ADD EMPTY**) instead, and the new slot goes on the first free pattern number, one that does not exist yet: an empty slot, so a new section starts from silence, not from a copy. If the pattern pool is full the strip says **NO FREE PATTERN** and nothing is written. `F8` (**UNDO**) takes the slot back. New in track3r-os.

On the TIMELINE page the blocks of sharing slots wear the same `*` at the right of the number.

To split them, put the cursor on the slot and press `F5` (**UNIQUE**). It gets a copy at the first free pattern number, with the same name, lengths and steps, and the strip says, for example, **SLOT 04: PATTERN 05 (A COPY OF 04)**. `Shift` + `Insert` (**DUP PAT**) adds a new slot with a copy straight away. `Note` jumps to the next slot that holds the cursor's pattern, and `Shift` + `Note` to the previous.

Example: the second verse should have other drums. Put the cursor on it, press `F5`, then edit pattern 5 in Pattern. The first verse is unchanged. `F8` (**UNDO**) takes the copy back.

### The track map

Press `Right` on the PAT column. The cursor moves into a grid: slots down, tracks across. A cell is one track of that slot's pattern. `Left` on track 1 returns to PAT.

The list draws 12 tracks at a time, each cell 20 pixels wide. A project with more tracks scrolls them with the cursor: the **TRACKS** caption then says which ones you see, for example **TRACKS 5-16**.

A muted track's cells are dim, so you see which tracks sound where you look. A solo does not dim them: only the mute does. New in track3r-os.

- `Shift` + arrows select a block of slots and tracks.
- `Copy` copies it (up to 32 cells). `Shift` + `Copy` pastes at the cursor, or tiles the clip over a selection. A paste never adds slots, and it never changes a track's length: steps past the end of a shorter track are dropped (**PASTED: 1 PATTERN, CLIPPED AT TRACK END**). A slot whose pattern does not exist yet gets a new one; if the pool is full the strip says **NO FREE PATTERN** and nothing is written.
- `Delete` clears the cells. `Shift` + `Delete` cuts them.
- If the block covers two or more patterns, `Delete` (and the cut) first asks on the strip: **CLEAR 3 PATTERNS?: F1 YES, OTHER KEY CANCELS**. `F1` clears them as one step that `F8` takes back; any other key leaves the cells as they were (a cut then leaves the clipboard as it was too; it fills on `F1`). The TOOLS dialog's CLEAR does not ask again after its own `F1`. One pattern is cleared at once. New in track3r-os.
- `F6` (**TOOLS**) opens a dialog over the block: **TRANSPOSE**, **INSTRUMENT**, **CLEAR**, **EXPORT WAV**, **FORM** and **BRIDGE**. `F1` applies, `F8` leaves.
- **FORM** builds the shape of a song from one to three patterns in one go, by taking things away: the first slot is the pattern with some tracks cleared (LOOP>SONG: the music, so drums only; POP: the kick and the rest of the drums, so music only; TECHNO: everything but the kick), a break is the pattern without the kick. Select the slots whose patterns you want (up to three different ones: A, B, C in the order of the slots; with fewer, the missing ones are A), open TOOLS, turn OP to **FORM**, choose **LOOP>SONG** (8 slots), **POP** (9) or **TECHNO** (10) and set **DRUMS**, how many tracks from track 1 are drums (the kick is track 1, the music is the tracks after the drums). The footer says the plan, for example `FROM 02 05 07  8 SLOTS  3 NEW PATTERNS`. `F1` puts the new slots after your selection (nothing you built moves or changes) and the cursor on the first of them; the changed versions are new patterns, so your originals are never touched. If the song, the pattern pool or the undo memory cannot take it, the strip says why (`SONG FULL: NEEDS 8 SLOTS, 7 FREE`, `NEEDS 3 FREE PATTERNS, 1 FREE`, `TOO BIG TO UNDO: SELECT LESS`) and nothing is written. One `F8` takes the slots and the new patterns back. It works while the song plays. New in the Community OS.
- **BRIDGE** puts a run of new slots between two neighbouring slots, so the music moves from the first pattern (A) to the second (B) instead of jumping. Put the cursor on A (B is the slot after it) or select exactly two slots, open TOOLS, turn OP to **BRIDGE** and set **SLOTS**, how many new slots (1 to 16, `Shift` turns it by 4). The footer says the plan, for example `PATTERN 02 TO 05  4 SLOTS  4 NEW PATTERNS`. `F1` makes each new slot a new pattern, `BRIDGE 1/4`, `BRIDGE 2/4` and so on: in the first one most steps are still A's, in the last most are B's, and in between the steps change from A's to B's a few at a time (always a whole step, never a note of A with the instrument of B; once a step has become B's it stays B's in the later slots; empty steps move like notes, so a note of A that B lacks thins out and a note of B that A lacks fills in). The tracks do not all start together and the steps of a track change one by one, which makes a gradual change. Every track is bridged, whatever the tracks you had selected. A short track repeats as it plays; when A and B have different lengths the tracks keep A's length up to the middle of the bridge and B's after it. The same A and B always give the same result. The cursor goes to the first new slot, A and B are never touched, and the refusals are FORM's, plus `SELECT 2 SLOTS`, `NO NEXT SLOT` (the cursor is on the last slot) and `SAME PATTERN IN BOTH SLOTS`. One `F8` takes the slots and the new patterns back. It works while the song plays. New in the Community OS.

An edit writes into the patterns, not into the slots. If a pattern is also held by a slot outside the block, nothing is written. The strip asks, for example, **PATTERN 06 ALSO IN 2 SLOTS: F1 ALL, F2 UNIQUE**. `F1` changes the pattern for every slot. `F2` copies it first and edits only the copy. Any other key, or 4 s, takes the question back with nothing written.

Each edit is one undo step with `F8`. An edit too big for the undo memory is refused: **TOO BIG TO UNDO: SELECT LESS**.

### The pads

`Shift` + `F7` (**PADS**) switches the 48 pads. The strip says **PADS: SLOTS** or **PADS: TRACKS**. TRACKS is the default at power-on. Rows 2 to 4 mute a track, cycle its mute mode and solo it, as on Pattern.

In SLOTS mode pad n is slot n of the 48-slot page that holds the cursor. When stopped, a pad moves the cursor. While the song plays, it queues that slot as a jump. A tap on the queued slot cancels it.

> **Careful**: In TRACKS mode a stray pad tap on Song mutes a track, and the mute is an undo step of Song.

(Picture: Song, map: slots 1 to 3 and tracks 1 to 3 are selected, and the strip counts what was copied.)

## Try it

1. Press `Song`. The list shows the slots, with the cursor on the first.

   (Picture: Song, LIST page: the slots with their pattern numbers; the NAME column is empty until a pattern is named.)

2. Press `Shift` + `Insert`. A new slot appears with a copy of the pattern. The info line says **SHIFT+INS DUP**.

   (Picture: Song: a second slot holds the copy.)

3. Press `F3` (**ADD SLOT**). The new slot holds the same pattern number. A `*` marks the two slots, and the info line says **pattern nn in 2 slots**.

   (Picture: Song: two slots share a pattern, marked with a star.)

4. Press `F5` (**UNIQUE**). The slot gets its own copy and the strip says **A COPY OF**.

   (Picture: Song: the strip reports the copy made for the slot.)

5. Press `Song` again. The **TIMELINE** page draws the same slots as blocks as wide as they have bars. Press `Song` once more to come back to the list, where **BAR** and **BARS** give each slot's start and length.

   (Picture: Song, TIMELINE page: each slot as a block as wide as it has bars.)

6. Press `F8` (**UNDO**). The slot points at the shared pattern again.

## The screen at a glance

(Picture: Song: the Shift row while Shift is held, with the quarter jumps, NAME, PADS and REDO.)

| Area | What it shows |
|---|---|
| Main area | The list: **POS**, **PAT**, **NAME** (12 characters), **BAR** (the bar the slot starts at), **BARS** (its length in bars) and the `*` mark. The track map sits to the right. The info line gives the slot, the bars in all and, for a shared pattern, **pattern nn in n slots**. |
| Timeline | The slots as blocks as wide as they have bars, with the pattern's number and a strip in its colour, and a lane per track under them that shows how many notes the track plays, and a thin **ENERGY** row at the foot. The info line gives the cursor's slot, its start bar, its pattern and its length; while the song plays it gives the bars left before the next slot instead (see "Read the song on the Timeline page"). |
| Info line | A note on the last key, or on the cursor's slot or track. |
| Strip | Messages, for example **PATTERN 03 NAMED**. |
| Key row | `F1` to `F8`. See the table under "Keys on this screen". |
| Shift row | **0/4** to **3/4** and **END** jump the cursor; `F6` **NAME**, `F7` **PADS**, `F8` **REDO**. |

## More tasks

### Move a slot

Start on Song, with the cursor on the slot.

1. Hold `Copy`, and press `Up` or `Down`.
2. Hold the arrow to keep moving. Each step is one undo step. `Shift` + arrows first select a range, and the range moves as a block.

You should see the slot change place, with the cursor following it. It works while the song plays.

### Cut and paste slots

Start on Song, with the cursor on PAT.

1. Press `Shift` + `Delete`. The strip says **CUT 1 SLOT**.
2. Move the cursor. Press `Shift` + `Copy`. The slots come back at the cursor.

Cutting every slot is refused: **SONG NEEDS A SLOT**.

### Name a pattern

Start on Song, with the cursor on the slot.

1. Press `Shift` + `F6` (**NAME**). The keyboard opens, titled **PATTERN NAME**.
2. Type with the pads, up to 30 characters, and press `F1` (**OK**). `F8` (**CANCEL**) keeps the old name.

You should see **PATTERN nn NAMED** in the strip. The NAME column shows it for every slot that holds the pattern.

### Delete a slot

Start on Song, with the cursor on the slot.

1. Press `Delete` or `F4` (**DEL SLOT**). One slot goes, even if you hold the key.

### Read the song on the Timeline page

New in track3r-os. The Timeline page shows the song as you would draw it on paper: one block for each slot, as wide as the slot is long. It helps you see where the long parts and the short parts are, and which tracks are busy where.

Start on Song.

1. Press `Song` until the header says **TIMELINE 2/2**. The blocks run from four slots before the cursor.
   A slot is as wide as it has bars (a bar is 16 steps). The page is always at least 16 bars wide, so a short song stays small and does not stretch.
2. Look at the blocks. Each one carries its pattern's number, and under the number a short strip in the pattern's colour: there are four colours, so patterns 1 and 5 share one. The strip tells you when a pattern comes back; the number tells you which it is. A very narrow block (one bar in a long view) may be too small for a three-digit number. A slot whose pattern does not exist yet has a dim number and no strip. A block whose pattern another slot also holds wears a `*` at the right of its number, as the list's rows do.
3. Look under the blocks. This is the note map: each track has a lane, and each slot shows a small tick for every step that holds a note, sixteen steps to a bar. You see the rhythm of each track, not only how busy it is. A step with only a volume, an effect or a note-off has no tick. A track that is shorter than the pattern stops where it stops. Patterns of different lengths use the same step width, so the ticks of a short and a long pattern line up with the bars. The ticks follow your edits in Pattern: edit one pattern and only its map changes. A slot whose pattern does not exist yet has no map.
4. Press `Left` or `Right`. The cursor moves one slot and the white frame follows it. The info line says, for example, **timeline slot 02 bar 5 pattern 02 4 bars**.
5. Press `Play`. A green bar under a block and a white line mark the slot and the step that play.
   The info line now counts down: **timeline NEXT IN 2 BARS cursor slot 02**. It counts the bars left in the pattern that plays, and the last bar says **1 BAR**.
   When you queue a jump (put the cursor on another slot with `Left` or `Right`, then press `Rec`) it says **JUMP IN**. On the last slot, where the song starts again at slot 0, it says **LOOP IN**; a single pattern playing says **LOOP IN** too. Stop, and the line goes back to the cursor's slot.
6. Look at the thin row **ENERGY** at the foot of the page. It has one column for each slot, as high as the slot is busy and loud: for each track, how many notes it plays, times how loud they are, times the track's volume. A muted track adds nothing, and while a track is soloed only the soloed tracks add. The tallest slot in view fills the row, so the curve shows the shape of the song around the cursor, not a level you can compare between two views.

The page draws the tracks Pattern can show, at most 12, and at most 40 slots and 48 bars: with 12 tracks it shows 34 slots. The cursor's slot is always in view.

### Edit on the Timeline page

New in track3r-os. The Timeline page is an editing grid. It uses the list's map with the arrows turned: `Left` and `Right` walk the slots, `Up` and `Down` the tracks. The row of blocks is the whole slot; a lane is one track of one slot, a cell.

Start on the Timeline page.

1. Press `Down`. The cursor drops into lane 1 of the slot: the cell has a box and the lane's number is bright. `Up` on lane 1 goes back to the blocks.
2. `Left` and `Right` keep the lane and move the slot. `Shift` + `Left` or `Right` select slots, `Shift` + `Up` or `Down` tracks; the block of cells you chose is on a band.
3. `Copy`, `Shift` + `Copy`, `Delete`, `Shift` + `Delete`, `F5` (**UNIQUE**) and `F6` (**TOOLS**) do what they do in the list's map, including the questions on the strip. On the blocks they act on whole slots, as on PAT.
4. Hold `Copy` and press `Left` or `Right` to move the slot along the song.

The cursor is shared with the list: turn the page and it stays on the same slot and track. The Timeline has 12 lanes, so track 13 to 16 are edited on the list.

### Look at Song and come back

Start on any other screen.

1. Hold `Song`. After 0.4 s the Song screen comes up. It opens on the page you left it on, for example **TIMELINE 2/2**.
2. Let go. You return to the screen you came from, as you left it.

## Keys on this screen

The key row, and the row drawn while `Shift` is held. `-` means the key does nothing.

| Key | Label | With `Shift` |
|---|---|---|
| `F1` | **PLAY PAT** | **0/4** |
| `F2` | **DUP PAT** | **1/4** |
| `F3` | **ADD SLOT** | **2/4** |
| `F4` | **DEL SLOT** | **3/4** |
| `F5` | **UNIQUE** | **END** |
| `F6` | **TOOLS** | **NAME** |
| `F7` | **TEMPO** | **PADS** |
| `F8` | **UNDO** | **REDO** |

| Key | What it does | Ref |
|---|---|---|
| `F1` (**PLAY PAT**) | play the slot's pattern in a loop; `Play` plays the song from the selected slot | QA-SNG-043 |
| `F2` (**DUP PAT**) | a slot after the cursor with a copy of the pattern, the same as `Shift` + `Insert` | QA-SNG-212 |
| `F1` (**PREVIEW**) in a lane of TIMELINE | loop the slot's pattern with only the rectangle's tracks sounding; `F1` again, `Stop` or leaving the screen ends the audition and restores the solo set; not an undo unit | QA-SNG-203, QA-SNG-204, QA-SNG-205, QA-SNG-206 |
| hold `F2` | loop the selected slots; the same slots again take the loop back | QA-SNG-200, QA-SNG-201 |
| `F3` (**ADD SLOT**), `Insert` | add a slot with the same pattern | QA-SNG-050 |
| hold `Copy` + `F3` (**ADD EMPTY**) | add a slot on the first free pattern (an empty one); **NO FREE PATTERN** when the pool is full | QA-SNG-211 |
| `F4` (**DEL SLOT**) | removes one slot, in the list and in the map too | QA-SNG-012, QA-SNG-028 |
| `Delete` | removes one slot in the list. In the map it clears the cells of the selection instead | QA-SNG-012, QA-SNG-028 |
| `F5` (**UNIQUE**) | give a shared slot its own copy | QA-SNG-034 |
| `F6` (**TOOLS**) | open the block tools | QA-SNG-029 |
| `F7` (**TEMPO**) | put the encoder on the tempo (1 BPM a detent, `Shift` for 0.1); `F7` again taps the tempo, two taps under 1.5 s apart set it (40 to 800 BPM); `F8` takes the edit back | QA-SNG-062 |
| `F8` (**UNDO**) | undo the last Song edit | QA-SNG-013 |
| the encoder | change the slot's pattern number, or the tempo after `F7` | QA-SNG-062 |
| `Right`, `Left` | enter and leave the map, walk the tracks (on Timeline: `Down` and `Up`; `Left` and `Right` walk the slots) | QA-SNG-020, QA-SNG-021, QA-SNG-116 |
| `Shift` + arrows | select slots and tracks | QA-SNG-022 |
| `Copy`, `Shift` + `Copy` | copy, paste | QA-SNG-023, QA-SNG-024 |
| `Shift` + `Delete` | cut | QA-SNG-053 |
| hold `Copy` + `Up` or `Down` | move the slot or range (on Timeline: `Left` or `Right`) | QA-SNG-056, QA-SNG-133 |
| `Note`, `Shift` + `Note` | next and previous use of the pattern | QA-SNG-058 |
| `Rec` while playing | queue a jump to the cursor's slot | QA-SNG-043 |
| `Shift` + `F1` to `F5` | jump the cursor to a quarter and to the end | QA-SNG-002 |
| `Shift` + `F6` (**NAME**), `F7` (**PADS**), `F8` (**REDO**) | name the pattern, switch the pads, redo | QA-SNG-010, QA-SNG-040 |
| hold `Song` | peek at Song until you let go | QA-SNG-060 |

## Good to know

- `Song` acts when you let go of it, because it waits to see whether you hold it. A press of 0.4 s or more on Song does not turn the page.
- Coming back from a peek enters the screen again: a question open on File is closed.
- `Shift` + `F3` jumps to 2/4. It does not add a slot.
- **NO SUCH PATTERN YET** and **SONG IS EMPTY** are the strip's replies to a name on a slot with no pattern, or on an empty song.
- `Pattern` on Song opens the pattern of the slot under the cursor.
- Adding, deleting or moving slots while the song plays does not move the playhead: the marker follows its slot and the song goes on to the slot that came after it. Delete the slot that plays and its pattern finishes, then the slot that took its place plays. Delete the queued slot and the strip says **QUEUED SLOT DELETED**. New in track3r-os.
- `F8` undoes Song edits only. An empty Song undo says **NOTHING TO UNDO HERE**.
- New in track3r-os: the map, TOOLS, UNIQUE, the marks, cut, move, next use, the pads and the peek.
- Not checked against the original firmware: the keys and pages not named above.

## See also

- [Pattern](pattern.md): the notes of each pattern. A slot holds one.
- [Pattern tools](pattern_tools.md): the same block tools on a single pattern.
- [Perform](perform.md): play the pattern live, without writing it.
