# Export

Status: draft

Export writes what the unit plays to WAV files on the card, and the tools are spread over three screens: the EXPORT page of File, the TOOLS menu of Pattern and the TOOLS dialog of Song. Song, pattern and stems exports work as the official manual describes. The stems are one WAV for each audio track that plays a note, plus the DELAY, REVERB and MIX files. The files are named differently: `Export/<PROJECT>/<PROJECT>_Song0001.wav`, and a second render takes the next number instead of a new folder.  **OG PROJECT** writes a folder in the original firmware's project format and is marked EXPERIMENTAL. Not checked against the original firmware: whether an official unit opens it.

## What it is for

Export writes what the unit plays to files on the card, in the folder `Export/<PROJECT>`. You can export the whole song, some slots of the song, one pattern, a block of a pattern, or the separate tracks (stems). These exports are WAV files.

**OG PROJECT** writes a folder in the project format of the original firmware. It is **EXPERIMENTAL**. See the last section.

Exports never change the project. Starting an export stops the transport.

## How it works

An export is an offline render: the unit renders the song, a pattern or a block without playing it aloud and writes the result as 16-bit stereo, 44,100 Hz WAV files in `Export/<PROJECT>` on the card. Nothing is live. Your project is not changed.

While it runs, only `F8` (**CANCEL**) works. The pads, `Play`, `Rec` and the screen buttons do nothing; nothing is queued for later. Cancelling, or the end of the render, gives the keys back. A second export never writes over the first: it makes `_0002`.

Example: to bring one drum pattern into another program, choose **PATTERN nn** and press `F1`. To mix it there, choose **PATT STEMS nn** instead, and you get one file for each audio track that plays a note, plus the DELAY, REVERB and MIX files.

## Try it

This walk-through exports one pattern.

1. Press `File`. The File screen opens on the PROJECTS page.
2. Press `F7` (**EXPORT**). The EXPORT page opens with the cursor on the row you used last. Press `Up` until it stops on **SONG**, the first row.

   (Picture: File, EXPORT page: five rows, the cursor on SONG, F1 reads EXPORT.)
3. Press `Down`. The cursor is on **PATTERN nn**. The screen says what you get: the pattern once, with its tail. Turn the encoder to choose another pattern if the project has one.

   (Picture: File, EXPORT page: the cursor on PATTERN, the lines under the rows say what F1 will make.)
4. Press `F1` (**EXPORT**). A progress overlay shows while it renders.
5. When it ends, the strip says `SAVED EXPORT/<PROJECT>/<PROJECT>_P<n>_0001.WAV`. The file is on the card.

## The screen at a glance

(Picture: File, EXPORT page: the rows to choose from, and the file name that F1 will make.)

| Row | What `F1` makes |
|---|---|
| SONG | The whole song, as one WAV file. |
| PATTERN nn | The pattern nn, as one WAV file. |
| SONG STEMS | One WAV file for each audio track that plays a note, and the DELAY, REVERB and MIX files. |
| PATT STEMS nn | The same set, for the pattern nn. |
| OG PROJECT | A project folder in the original firmware's format. EXPERIMENTAL. |

The page is on the File screen, on the PROJECTS page, with `F7` (**EXPORT**). The card under the rows shows the file name `F1` will make. From the Pattern screen, the same WAV exports are pads of the TOOLS menu.

## More tasks

### Export a pattern from the EXPORT page

Start on the File screen, on the PROJECTS page.

1. Press `F7` (**EXPORT**), then `Up` until the cursor stops on **SONG**. The page keeps the row you used last.
2. Press `Down` to **PATTERN nn**. The nn starts at the pattern you were on.
3. Turn the encoder to the pattern you want. It moves to the next pattern that exists.
4. Press `F1` (**EXPORT**).

You should see `SAVED EXPORT/<PROJECT>/<PROJECT>_P<n>_0001.WAV` when it ends. Exporting again makes `_0002`, and never writes over the first file.

### Export the pattern on screen from the Pattern screen

Start on the Pattern screen, with the transport stopped.

1. Press `F7` (**TOOLS**). The verb menu opens. **EXPORT PAT** is pad 15 (with a block, **EXPORT SEL** is pad 14).
2. Press pad 15 (**EXPORT PAT**).

The file is `<PROJECT>_P<n>_0001.WAV`, as on the EXPORT page.  It opens in STEP and WATCH while the transport plays; only in LIVE it does not open and the strip says **THE PLAYHEAD HOLDS THE CURSOR IN LIVE** — leave LIVE, then press `F7`.

### Export a block of the pattern

Start on the Pattern screen, in **STEP**.

1. Select the block with `Shift` and the arrows.
2. Press `F7` (**TOOLS**). The verb menu opens, with **EXPORT SEL** on pad 14, next to **EXPORT PAT**.
3. Press pad 14 (**EXPORT SEL**).

You should see `SAVED EXPORT/<PROJECT>/<PROJECT>_SEL0001.WAV`. The file holds only the tracks of the block, from its first row to the end of its last row. The other tracks are muted in the file. A block that covers only some columns of a track still exports that track's whole steps.

> **Tip**: The selection ends at the first silence after the block. **EXPORT PATTERN** keeps the tail of its reverb and delay.

### Export some slots of the song

Start on the Song screen. The transport may be playing: the export stops it.

1. Pick the slots. With the cursor on **PAT**, `Shift` + `Down` or `Up` extends a range of slots. With no range, the export takes the slot under the cursor.
2. In the track map, `Shift` + `Left` or `Right` also picks tracks. With no range of tracks or slots selected, the export takes every track. A range of slots with no range of tracks, picked in the map, renders only the track under the cursor.
3. Press `F6` (**TOOLS**). On the **OP** row, turn the encoder, or press `Left` or `Right`, to **EXPORT WAV**. The row below it goes, and the footer names the slots and the tracks.
4. Press `F1` (**APPLY**).

The progress overlay reads **EXPORTING THE SLOTS**. You should see `SAVED EXPORT/<PROJECT>/<PROJECT>_S<a>-<b>_0001.WAV`. The numbers are the Song screen's slot numbers, so the first slot is `S0`. A second export of the same slots is `_0002`, and nothing is written over.

The file runs from the first slot to the end of the last, then keeps the tail of the delay and the reverb, as the song export does. It holds the tracks you picked, or every track. A muted or soloed track you picked does sound. If the slots hold an Order jump that goes back inside them, the export loops as the song does, until it stops with `TOO LONG FOR A WAV (100 MIN)`; `F8` (**CANCEL**) stops it sooner.

> **Tip**: The SONG row of the EXPORT page is not changed. It still writes the whole song as `<PROJECT>_Song0001.WAV`.

### Export the stems

Start on the File screen, on the EXPORT page.

1. Press `Up` until the cursor stops on **SONG**, then `Down` three times to **PATT STEMS nn**. For the song, press `Up` once, to **SONG STEMS**.
2. For a pattern, turn the encoder to the pattern you want.
3. Press `F1` (**EXPORT**).

You should see `SAVED n STEMS` when it ends. The files are `<PROJECT>_P<n>_S0001_T01.wav` and so on, then `_DELAY`, `_REVERB` and `_MIX`. For the song, the name uses `Song` in place of `P<n>`.

Which files a set has: one track file for each audio track that plays a note. A track with no notes, a MIDI track and a MIDI instrument have no file. DELAY and REVERB appear only when that bus can sound. MIX is always there, and it is the last file.

All the files of a set have the same length. A second set gets the next number, `S0002`, and it never writes over the first set.

### Cancel an export

1. Press `F8` (**CANCEL**) while the progress overlay is up.

The strip says **EXPORT CANCELLED**, or `CANCELLED: n OF m STEMS SAVED` for a set. The files already finished stay on the card. The file being written is not left on the card.

### Export the project for the original firmware (EXPERIMENTAL)

Start on the File screen, on the EXPORT page.

1. Press `Down` until the cursor stops on **OG PROJECT**, the last row. The row reads **EXPERIMENTAL**.
2. Read the card. It shows the folder name, the size, and the list **LOSES**. The list says what the export would leave out. While it says **COUNTING...**, there is no size or list yet.
3. Press `F1` (**EXPORT**). If something would be left out, the strip says `LOSES <n kinds>: F1 AGAIN`. Press `F1` again to go on. If the count is not done, the strip says `COUNTING WHAT THE EXPORT LOSES: WAIT`, and `F1` starts nothing.
4. Wait for the end. The strip says **SAVED**, and it names any kinds that were not kept.

You should see the folder `Export/<NAME> OG` on the card. A second export makes `<NAME> OG 2`, and so on up to `OG 99`. Nothing already on the card changes.

> **Careful**: `F8` stops the export. The finished files stay, but there is no project file until the last file is done. The folder is then not a project.

The export asks first only when something would be left out. Any other key, a move, leaving the screen or waiting 4 seconds takes the question back. If the project changes while the question is up, `F1` counts again and asks with the new count.

The export refuses while a take is armed or recording, while a job, a load or a save runs, and on a card it cannot write (no card, a write-protected card or an exFAT card). Any other SD card with a FAT volume works. The strip gives the reason, and no folder is made. `F1` stops the transport before it starts.

## Keys on this screen

| Key | What it does |
|---|---|
| `File` | Opens the File screen. |
| `F7` (**EXPORT**) | On the PROJECTS page, opens the EXPORT page.  |
| `Up`, `Down` | Choose a row. They stop at the first and the last row.  |
| encoder | On PATTERN and PATT STEMS, moves to the next pattern that exists. On the song rows it does nothing.  |
| `Shift` + encoder | On PATTERN, moves eight patterns a turn.  |
| `F1` (**EXPORT**) | Starts the chosen row.  |
| `F8` (**CANCEL**) | Stops an export. The finished files stay.  |
| `F7` (**TOOLS**), on Pattern | Opens the verb menu; EXPORT PAT is pad 15, and EXPORT SEL is pad 14 when a block is selected.  |
| `F6` (**TOOLS**), on Song | Opens the dialog over the selected slots. Its fourth OP is **EXPORT WAV**, and `F1` (**APPLY**) starts it.  |

While an export runs, only `F8` works.

## Good to know

- A WAV file is 16-bit stereo at 44,100 Hz. It plays as the unit plays it: tempo, swing, effects, the delay and reverb tails, and the limiter.
- A WAV file does not hold live input, the USB return, the pads or MIDI notes.
- A project with no folder is exported as `Untitled`; the strip shows it in capitals.
- The stems add up to the MIX only while the limiter does nothing. A mix the limiter works on is not the sum of its stems.
- If an export fails, the strip says `EXPORT FAILED` and the reason. No file is left under its final name, and no temporary file either. The files you already had are not touched.
- Holding `Power` during an export does not stop it at once. The strip says **EXPORT RUNNING - HOLD POWER AGAIN TO STOP IT**. A second hold within 10 seconds stops it, and the finished files stay. See [The panel](panel.md#power).
- The EXPORT page stays open when you leave the File screen.

**OG PROJECT** has its own rules:

- The original firmware's format is checked byte for byte against reference files. Whether an official unit opens the folder is an open research question.
- The OS opens its own export again. It does not restore the pattern names.
- Channel Pan is dropped, and the export counts it.
- A sample at 22,050 Hz, 16,726 Hz, 8,287 Hz or in the Amiga engine is written at 44,100 Hz, with its pitch kept.
- A project made on the older level law keeps the gain of its instruments. Under -24 dB, the level is limited and the question counts it.
- The question can name 15 kinds: sample instruments with no file, instruments with no sample memory ready, 12 bit and 8 bit engine instruments, Amiga engine instruments, instruments too long for a file, levels clamped, module instruments, effect and volume columns, steps on tracks 13 to 16, track settings (pan, solo, bus), MIDI instruments and settings, sample instruments in slots 49 to 64, Sine LFO shapes, names cut short, and other settings, names and rates.  A Sine LFO is written as Triangle, and the question counts it as `1 SINE LFO`.  The list shows up to three kinds, one line each. With more, it shows every kind in a short form, run together; FX and modules are always named.
- MIDI lane events (see [Pattern](pattern.md)) have no place in the original format. They are left out of the pattern files, and the question and the report say **LANE EVENTS NOT EXPORTED** with their number (the strip: `n LANES`). The other files are the same as for a project with no lanes. New in track3r-os.
- After an export, `diag ogexp status` also says where its time went: the slowest step with its stage, then the time of each stage. It changes no file and no screen.

## See also

- [File](file.md): saving, opening and the project folder on the card.
- [Pattern](pattern.md): the Pattern screen, where EXPORT PATTERN and EXPORT SELECTION start.
- [Song](song.md): the Song screen, where EXPORT WAV of slots starts.
- [Fill and tools](pattern_tools.md): the TOOLS menu in full.

---

# Effects in the pattern

Status: draft

Each step has two effect cells, FX1 and FX2, next to the note, and an effect changes how that note plays: a chord, an arpeggio, a slide, a drive or a volume change. The list holds effects 0 to 42, which are the original layout's ids (Chord, Arp, Tune, Slides, Overdrive and Bit Depth among them), and at its end 17 tracker effects. A tracker effect starts at a sensible default, and the info line reads the value in words. New in track3r-os: the 17 tracker effects.  Not checked against the original firmware: how the first 43 read and behave.

## What it is for

Use a step effect when one note needs its own treatment and a new instrument would be too much. You come here from [Pattern](pattern.md): press `Rec` for **STEP**, then `Fx`.

## How it works

### A step FX: live, stored and ended

A step FX is a mark on one step, like "slide here" on a score. Two cells mean two effects can work together on one note.

- **Live:** the effect acts when the sequencer reaches the step, and the grid shows its name, letter or mark and its value in hex.
- **Stored:** in the pattern, on that step, exactly as written. The FX stay as written even when the instrument is a module.
- **Ended:** most effects end with their step. **Panning** ends with its step. **Channel Pan** stays on the track until another Channel Pan, or until you stop and play again. Stop also gives channel and global volumes back, so the pads sound at full level.

### The value

The value sets how strong the effect is. The grid shows it in hex and the info line reads it in words, for example `DRIVE 40 %`. A new effect starts at its own default: Tune starts at 0 semitones. If a cell has an effect and you change its type, the value stays, cut to the new range.

(Picture: Pattern, STEP mode: the info line reads CHORD 5A for the effect under the cursor, in words.)

### Two effects that work together: Chord and Arp

A **Chord** on a MIDI track sounds all its notes at once. An **Arp** plays them one at a time, a note every 8 steps down to every 1/8 step. Example: a C note with Chord 5 (major) in FX1 and Arp 6 in FX2 plays C, then E, then G, one a step. With no Chord, an Arp changes nothing. On a sample track the Arp restarts the sample at each new pitch.

## Try it

1. Press `Pattern`, then `Rec` (**STEP**), then `Fx`. The cursor is on FX1 of step 1.

   (Picture: Pattern, STEP mode: the cursor is on the first effect cell of step 1.)

2. Hold `Vol`. The effect list opens with a description under it. Turn the encoder 14 detents to **Reverse**.

   (Picture: Pattern: the FX list is open and Reverse is highlighted, with its description under the list.)

3. Let go of `Vol`. The cell shows the effect's three-letter name, **REV**.
4. Turn the encoder up. The value stops at its last value, 01, and does not wrap.

   (Picture: Pattern: FX1 of step 1 reads REV01.)

5. Press `Fx` again. The cursor moves to FX2, and FX1 keeps its effect.

   (Picture: Pattern: the cursor is on the second effect cell, FX1 reads REV01.)

6. Press `Play` and listen to step 1: Reverse sets the direction the sample plays in.

## The screen at a glance

| Area | What it shows |
|---|---|
| Fx column | Two effect cells per step, FX1 and FX2. Each shows the effect and its value in hex. At the 5-track zoom the effect is its three-letter name, for example `CHD` for Chord. An effect without a name, and the cells of the older zooms, show a letter or a mark.  |
| Info line | The effect under the cursor, in words, after the mode chip. For example `CHORD 5A`. |
| Effect list | The list of effects, shown while you hold `Vol`. The newest effects are at the end. |

## More tasks

### Set a big value

1. Hold `Shift` and turn the encoder. The value moves 16 at a time.

The value stops at its first and last value. It does not wrap around.

### Clear an effect

Start on the Pattern screen, in **STEP**, on the step with the effect.

1. Hold `Vol`. The effect list opens.
2. Turn the encoder to **None**.
3. Let `Vol` go. The cell is empty.

To clear the effects of several steps at once, put the cursor on **FX1** and press `Shift` + `Down` for each extra step. Press `Shift` + `Right` once more to add **FX2**, then `Delete`. The note and volume stay, and one `F8` (**UNDO**) takes it back. New in track3r-os.

### Play a chord as an arpeggio

Start on the Pattern screen, in **STEP**, on a step with a C note. Use a MIDI track or a sample track.

1. Put **Chord** in FX1 with the value 5. The value 5 is a major chord, 4 is a minor chord.
2. Put **Arp** with the value 6 in the other effect cell. The value 6 plays the chord up, one note a step.
3. Press `Play`. The notes C, E and G play one after another, one a step.

### Look up an effect with words for its value

These effects read their value in words on the info line.

| Effect | What it does | Info line, with an example value |
|---|---|---|
| Chord | Plays the note as a chord. Value 5 is major, 4 is minor. | `CHORD 5A` for value 8  |
| Arp | Plays a chord one note at a time. It needs a Chord in the other cell. | `ARP DOWN 4 STEPS` for value 14  |
| Tune | Moves the note in semitones. Value 24 is no change. | `TUNE +7 ST` for value 31  |
| Slide Up, Slide Down | Slides the pitch over the step. The value is sixteenths of a semitone. | `SLIDE UP 2.19 ST` for value 35  |
| Glide | Slides from the last note on the track to this one. Value 0 is off. | `GLIDE 240 MS` for value 12  |
| Overdrive | Drives the sound. Value 0 is clean. | `DRIVE 40 %` for value 40  |
| Bit Depth | Lowers the bit depth. The range is 1 to 16, and 16 is off. | `BITS 8` for value 8  |
| Chance | Decides per pass whether the step plays. 0..100 is a probability, 101..174 a condition (below). | `CHANCE 50 %` for value 50  |
| Panning | Pans the note. Value 100 is hard right. It ends with its step. |  |
| Volume LFO, Panning LFO, Finetune LFO, Position LFO | Start the track's LFO for the volume (tremolo), the pan (auto-pan), the pitch (vibrato) or the wavetable window or granular position, on a sampler instrument. These four did nothing before; they act now, as Filter LFO does. The value is the LFO's speed in the same list as the instrument's own LFO speed, from the slowest at 0: 0 to 23 for Volume LFO, 0 to 28 for the others. The shape and amount are the instrument's LFO for that target (an instrument with none: triangle, 50 %). Position LFO moves only a wavetable or granular instrument and does nothing on a plain sample. While a Perform LFO row is held on the track its speed wins, and the FX comes back when the row ends or is at 0. Panning LFO and Panning (31) on one track: while the LFO runs it wins, because it sets the pan every block (a Panning step after it is overridden too); when the LFO ends the instrument's pan is back, and Panning acts again at its next step. The LFO stops at the next transport start. Stop does not end it: a pad note played after Stop still gets the LFO until the next Play. |  |

### Chance: what plays and what does not

**Chance** on a step decides, once per pass of the pattern, whether that step plays at all. The value is a probability or a condition.

| Value | What it means | Info line, with an example value |
|---|---|---|
| 0..100 | The step plays with that probability: 0 never, 50 half the passes, 100 always. | `CHANCE 50 %` for value 50 |
| 101 | Plays when the track's last Chance condition fired. | `CHANCE WITH LAST` |
| 102 | Plays when it did not. | `CHANCE NOT LAST` |
| 103..138 | Play N passes, then skip M (N and M 1..6, counted in passes of the pattern). 103 is Play 1 / Skip 1: the step plays on every other pass. | `CHANCE PLAY 2 SKIP 3` for value 111 |
| 139..174 | Skip N passes, then play M. | `CHANCE SKIP 6 PLAY 6` for value 174 |

The encoder walks every value from 0 to 174. `Shift` + encoder walks 0..100, then 101, 102, 103, then by 6. The pads and a **Fill** with MODE RANDOM write 0..100 only; a Fill with CONSTANT or FROM..TO reaches 174. Fill RANDOM on Chance with FROM above 100 draws 100. A step whose Chance does not fire plays nothing of its own: no note, no effect of the step. New in track3r-os.

### Look up a tracker effect

The tracker effects are at the end of the list, after Bit Depth. Each has a mark in the grid. Their values are hex.

| Effect | Mark | Value | Info line, with an example value |
|---|---|---|---|
| Tracker Arp | `@` | 37 | `ARPEG +3 +7`. Value 00 is `ARPEG OFF`.  |
| Volume Slide | `^` | 04 | `VSLIDE -4`. Value 40 is `VSLIDE +4`.  |
| Fine Volume Slide | `~` | 30 | `FVOL +3`  |
| Fine Porta Up | `<` | 10 | `FINE UP 4.00 PER`  |
| Fine Porta Down | `>` | 01 | `FINE DOWN 0.25 PER`  |
| Pan Slide | `=` | 04 | `PANSL R 4`  |
| Vibrato Wave | `"` | 02 | `VIB SQUARE`. Waves are 0 sine, 1 ramp, 2 square, 3 random.  |
| Tremolo Wave | `'` | 07 | `TREM RANDOM NORETRIG`  |
| Glissando | `;` | 01 | `GLISS ON`. Value 00 is `GLISS OFF`.  |
| Retrigger | `/` | 23 | `RETRIG EVERY 3 VOL -2`  |
| Tremor | `:` | 21 | `TREMOR ON 3 OFF 2`  |
| Channel Pan | `\|` | 4B | `CHPAN 75`. 50 is the centre.  |
| Channel Volume | `[` | 20 | `CHVOL 32`. 64 is full.  |
| Channel Vol Slide | `]` | 04 | `CHVSL -4`  |
| Global Volume | `(` | 30 | `GVOL 48`. 64 is full.  |
| Global Vol Slide | `)` | 40 | `GVSL +4`  |
| Panbrello | `{` | 3A | `PANBR SPD 3 DEP 10`  |

### Shape the envelopes and the grain length: w, y and z

New in track3r-os, from the tracker-ce step effects `w`, `y` and `z`. They sit after the core effects in the list (96, 97, 98). Each acts on the instrument's own settings for this note and ends at the first row that does not hold it.

| Effect | Mark | Value | What it does | Info line, with an example value |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Amp Envelope | `w` | 88 | The high digit scales the amp envelope's duration, the low digit warps it (8 is none, 0 to 15). On an amp ADSR the digits are the attack and the decay. | `AMP ENV x8 WARP +0` for 88 |
| Filter Envelope | `y` | 24 | The cutoff envelope's attack (high digit x 8 ms, at least 1) and decay (low digit x 8 ms). | `FLT ENV 16/32 MS` for 24 |
| Grain Length | `z` | 32 | The grain length of a granular instrument, 0 to 100 (hex 00 to 64): 0 is 44 samples, 50 is 100 ms, 100 is 1 s, never longer than the sample. It acts when the next grain starts. FX1 wins over FX2 when both hold a z. The value is hex: 32 is 50. | `GRAIN 100 MS` for 32 (the start value) |

`z` does nothing on an instrument that is not granular.

## Keys on this screen

| Key | What it does |
|---|---|
| `Fx` | Selects the Fx column on FX1. Press it again to move to FX2.  |
| hold `Vol` | Opens the effect list. Let go to enter the effect that is highlighted.  |
| encoder | Changes the value of the effect in the cell. While `Vol` is held, it moves through the list.  |
| `Shift` + encoder | Steps the value by 16. It stops at the first and last value.  |
| `F8` (**UNDO**) | Takes back the last change, with the other Pattern edits. A Song or Params edit stays. When nothing is left, the strip says **NOTHING TO UNDO HERE**.  |

## Good to know

- New in track3r-os: the tracker effects, from Tracker Arp to Panbrello.

- Writing a note by hand over a step that has a note replaces the note and its instrument with the ones in force. The volume and both effect cells stay. New in track3r-os.
- The tracker effects run once a tick and are built to add only a few tenths of a percent of processor time. Not yet measured on the unit.
- Stop gives the channel and global volumes back, so the pads sound at full level after a stop.
- The effect list has 60 entries.
- Not checked against the original firmware: the Chord and Arp readings. This is an open research question.

## See also

- [Pattern](pattern.md): notes, the record modes and the Fx column keys.
- [Fill and tools](pattern_tools.md): fill a track with notes by a rule.
- [Modules and apps](modules.md): which effects a module instrument obeys is in [Step FX on module instruments](module-instrument-fx.md).

# Input test

Status: draft

Input test is a hidden screen that draws every button, pad and turn of the encoder as the unit reads it, and counts them. No screen button and no Navigator entry opens it: you hold three keys while the unit turns on. While it is up, nothing acts on a key, so you can press everything, `Play` and `Song` included. This screen is new in track3r-os.

## What it is for

Use Input test to check that every key and pad of your unit answers, and how fast. Switch the unit off. Hold `Shift`, `F1` and `F8`, switch the unit on, and keep them down until the strip reads **INPUT TEST**. The picture starts clean, with every count at zero.

## The screen at a glance

| Area | What it shows |
|---|---|
| Strip, right side | `PADS OK  KEYS OK  ERR n  DROP n  FLT n  RSYNC n`. **OK** reads **NO** when a scanner does not answer. The other four are counters taken over from the input path.  |
| Buttons | 33 cells in 11 columns of 3, named as the keycaps: `F1`, `PAT`, `SHIFT`, `LEFT`.  |
| Button caption | `AGE x.x MS  MAX x.x MS  EVENTS n`: the age of the last event, the longest age seen, and the events counted.  |
| Pads | 48 cells in 12 columns of 4, each with its number in the corner. The caption reads `PADS  (0 = top left, 11 = top right)`.  |
| Encoder line | `ENCODER  TOTAL +n  LAST +n  EVENTS n`, dim until the first turn.  |
| Key row | `F2` and `F3` read **CLEAR**, `F4` and `F5` read **EXIT**. The rest are blank.  |

The pads are numbered from 0 here, not from 1 as in the rest of the manual: pad 0 is the top left, pad 11 the top right.

## More tasks

### Test the buttons

Start on Input test.

1. Press each button once, and hold one. The cell lights while the key is down.
2. Let go. The cell shows its count, `1` after one press. A cell you have not touched stays plain.
3. Press the same button again. The count reads `2`. A bounce in the key reads as `2` for one touch.

A press that the chip repeats counts once. The count stops at `99`.

### Test the pads and the encoder

1. Touch each pad, harder and softer. The cell lights while the pad is down and shows its count after.
2. Turn the encoder both ways. **TOTAL** is the sum of the clicks with its sign, **LAST** the last turn (`-2` for two clicks to the left) and **EVENTS** the number of turns.

### Start the counts again

1. Press `F2` and `F3` together. Every count, the encoder total and the event count go back to zero.

A key that is still down stays lit. `F2` or `F3` alone only light their own cell. Hold `Shift` while you clear to see a key stay lit.

### Leave Input test

1. Press `F4` and `F5` together. The unit goes to Pattern, and the keys work again: `Song` opens Song.

`F4` or `F5` alone are counted and do nothing.

## Keys on this screen

| Key | What it does | Ref |
|---|---|---|
| `F2` and `F3` together (**CLEAR**) | Sets every count to zero. A key that is down stays lit. | QA-INP-006 |
| `F4` and `F5` together (**EXIT**) | Leaves for Pattern. | QA-INP-007 |
| Any other key, pad or turn | Is drawn and counted. Nothing else happens. | QA-INP-008 |

## Good to know

- Nothing acts while the screen is up. `Song`, `File`, `Pattern`, `Master`, `Play` and the arrows only count. `Shift` + `Master` does not change the theme, and a pad selects no instrument. `F1`, `F6`, `F7` and `F8` alone do nothing.
- The age of an event runs from the scan of the key to the moment the app gets it. The error, drop and latency figures are real only on the unit.
- The screen cannot be reached in the simulator.

## See also

- [The panel](panel.md): the keys held at power-up, and what each opens.
- [Getting started](getting_started.md): the first boot and the screen layout.

---

# Instrument

Status: draft

Instrument gathers everything about one sound on five pages, SOURCE, VOICE, FILTER, MOD and SENDS on `F1` to `F5`, and puts copy, paste, delete and save on the Shift row. An empty slot opens a type chooser instead of a page. The PLAY ENGINE row picks how a sample is played, from the clean Modern engine down to the Amiga's 8-bit sound. The official manual has two parameter pages on the `Params` button. Here there are five pages on `F1` to `F5`, and `Left` and `Right` change the value of the row, like one click of the encoder.  Not checked against the original firmware: the Shift row and the type chooser.

## What it is for

Use Instrument to set how an instrument sounds and plays. Open it with the `Params` button. A project has 64 instrument slots. An empty slot opens the type chooser: **SAMPLE**, **MIDI**, **MODULE**, or a file to load.

## How it works

An instrument is one of the 64 slots of the project, and it is stored with the project. Every row you turn is live: the sound follows each step while a pad is held, and nothing waits for a confirm key.  Your edits are kept in the project when you save it, and `Shift` + `F5` (**SAVE**) writes a copy of a sample instrument to its own `.pti` file that other projects can load.

Nothing here "ends" by itself: a value stays until you change it. `Delete` puts the row under the cursor back to its default, `Shift` + `Delete` sets every row to its default, and `F8` (**UNDO**) takes back the last change. A sweep of the encoder on one row is one undo step, and a pause of 1.5 seconds starts a new one.

The pads play the instrument in view, so you hear each change while you hold a pad. `Shift` + pad plays it too (new Community OS behaviour), so you can hold `Shift` for the coarse step of the encoder and still tap the pads; the instrument itself changes with `F6` and `F7`.  Example: on a sample instrument, open the FILTER page, move to **CUTOFF**, hold a pad and turn the encoder. The filter closes under your finger, and one `F8` puts it back.

### The volume law

The **VOLUME** row (on the VOICE page) sets the level. The volume law turns it into decibels (dB). An older project keeps its loudness when saved and reloaded.

| Project | VOLUME 50 | VOLUME 100 |
|---|---|---|
| A native project, or an original-firmware project of version 7 or later | 0 dB | +24 dB |
| An original-firmware project below version 7 | about -20 dB | 0 dB |

If you want to know more: a module imported from a tracker file keeps its loudness; volume 64 becomes level 50, which is 0 dB (checked on the host). The Amiga engine gives the same dB as the Modern one.

Between the marked points, each step of **VOLUME** is 0.48 dB in the first law (volume 1 is -24 dB, and 0 is silence) and 0.4 dB in the second.

A project saved by an earlier build can sound at a different level, and the stored levels stay as they were. A note that names no velocity, on a native instrument at level 80, now plays at 0 dB; it played at +24 dB. On the Amiga engine levels 50 and 80 both play full volume. A module imported now gives its instruments velocity 63, so a Roll that fades with VolUp or VolDown peaks about 6 dB lower and sits 6 dB under a plain note. The demo kit stays at 0 dB after any edit.

### The play engine

The **PLAY ENGINE** row picks the engine for a sample: **Auto**, **Modern**, **Amiga**, **12-bit** or **8-bit**. **Auto** picks the Amiga engine for a **ONE SHOT** or **LOOP FWD** sample at the Paula rate, and the Modern engine for the rest. Paula is the Amiga's sound chip. Its rate here is 8,287 Hz (PAL) or 8,363 Hz (NTSC). The Amiga engine plays a sample as that chip does: it holds each value until the next one, and uses 8 bits of it. The **12-bit** and **8-bit** engines are the Modern engine with its output cut to 12 or 8 bits, and cap the **BIT DEPTH** row the same way.

The **STEREO** row under it says whether a sample plays as a stereo pair: **MONO** or **STEREO**. This is new in track3r-os. **STEREO** can only be chosen for a sample that was loaded with **STEREO** on Sample load (see [Sample load](sample_load.md)): on any other sample the row says `STEREO NEEDS A STEREO LOAD` and stays **MONO**. A **STEREO** instrument plays its two channels: the left output gets the mix plus the side signal, the right output the mix minus it, through the track's level and pan like any other sound.  A stereo note uses a little more of the unit's time than a mono one (about 0.8 percentage points of the audio budget each, not yet measured on the unit), so at most four voices play in stereo at once: the next one plays as the mix on both sides.

A note plays in stereo when its play mode plays forward (**ONE SHOT**, **LOOP FWD**, **SLICE**, **BEAT SLICE**) on the Modern engine, with no filter, **OVERDRIVE**, **BIT DEPTH** or tremolo on it. Otherwise it plays the mix: a backward or ping-pong loop, a wavetable, a granular instrument, the Amiga engine, a note played in reverse, or any of those effects. If one of the effects comes on while a stereo note sounds, the side signal fades out over one audio block (about 1.5 ms) and stays off for that note; the next note is stereo again. A track with its fader closed or muted drops the side signal too, for the rest of that note. The track's own outputs stay mono: the send effects, the CUE and REC buses, the meters and the USB track stems carry the mix; the master, the headphones and the USB main pair carry the stereo image.  Turning the row over while a note sounds takes effect at the next stop.

If you want to know more: a full-scale square wave on the Amiga engine peaks at +2.5 dB above its level. It matches a reference Amiga player on the host.

## Try it

This walk-through sweeps the filter of the instrument in view and takes the sweep back.

1. Press `Params`. The Instrument screen opens on the SOURCE page.
2. Press `F3` (**FILTER**). The cursor starts on **FILTER**, the first row.
3. Press `Down` twice. The cursor passes **FILTER TYPE** and is on **CUTOFF**, which reads **30 %** in the demo project.
4. Hold a pad and turn the encoder 20 clicks to the left. **CUTOFF** falls to **10 %** and the sound gets darker with each click.

   (Picture: Instrument, FILTER page: CUTOFF reads 10 %, and the curve rolls off early.)
5. Let go of the pad and press `F8` (**UNDO**). The whole sweep is taken back in one step: **CUTOFF** reads **30 %** again.

   (Picture: Instrument, FILTER page: CUTOFF is back at 30 %.)

Hold the pad again and the sound is as bright as before.

## The screen at a glance

(Picture: Instrument, SOURCE page of a sample: the header shows the play mode and engine, and F1 reads SAMPLE, the instrument's kind.)

| Area | What it shows |
|---|---|
| Header | The number and name, then the play mode and the engine, such as `05 BREAK_A` and `ONE SHOT / AUTO>MODERN`. A MIDI instrument shows its channel instead, such as `MIDI / CH 3`. The kind is the label of `F1`: **SAMPLE** (**WT**, **GRAIN** or **SLICE** for those play modes) or **MIDI**. |
| Rows | The settings of the page. The encoder changes the value under the cursor. |
| Strip | Short messages, such as `INS 03 DELETED - F8 UNDO`. |
| Key row | `F1` to `F5` open the pages. `F6` and `F7` change the instrument. `F8` is **UNDO**. |
| Shift row | **NAME**, **COPY**, **PASTE**, **DELETE**, **SAVE**, the nearest-instrument keys and **REDO**. |

## More tasks

### Set the play mode of a sample

Start on a sample instrument.

1. Press `Params`. The SOURCE page opens.
2. Press `Down` to **PLAY MODE**. Turn the encoder through ONE SHOT, LOOP FWD, LOOP BWD, PING-PONG, SLICE, BEAT SLICE, WAVETABLE and GRANULAR. It stops at each end.
3. Press `Delete` on **PLAY MODE** to go back to ONE SHOT.

You should see the rows of the new mode. The waveform on the right follows each edit: the start and end (and the loop), the slice lines, the wavetable window or the grain, such as `GRAIN 50.0 MS AT 1.373 s` or `WINDOW 20 OF 0..63`.

| Play mode | Rows under PLAY MODE |
|---|---|
| WAVETABLE | WT POS, WT SIZE |
| GRANULAR | GRAIN POS, GRAIN LENGTH, GRAIN SHAPE, GRAIN LOOP |
| SLICE, BEAT SLICE | SLICES, SLICE, PLAY THRU |

In **SLICE** and **BEAT SLICE**, **PLAY THRU** (the row after **SLICE**) turns play-through on: a slice then plays on through the following slices to the end of the sample, until the note ends or the sample does, instead of stopping at the next slice point; a note played in reverse starts at the sample end and runs down. It is `OFF` by default, one click of the encoder turns it `ON` (one undo step), and it is kept with the instrument when the project or the instrument is saved; in the other play modes the row is not there and the setting does nothing.

### Shape the sound: VOICE, FILTER and SENDS

Start on a sample instrument.

1. Press `F2` (**VOICE**). On the last row, **VEL>**, turn the encoder to scale the keyboard's velocity, 0 to 100 %. At 100 % (the default) velocity 64 plays as 64 of 127; at 50 %, as 96.
2. Press `F3` (**FILTER**), press `Down` twice to **CUTOFF**, and turn the encoder. A sweep is one undo step: `F8` (**UNDO**) takes it back. A pause of more than 1.5 seconds between two clicks starts a new step.
   While **FILTER** reads Off, **CUTOFF** and **RESONANCE** are dim and the info line says `FILTER OFF`: they still take the encoder, but you hear nothing until you turn the filter on.
3. Press `F5` (**SENDS**). Turn the encoder on **OVERDRIVE**. The sound saturates while the note plays; 0 is clean.

**VOLUME** and **GLIDE** are on the VOICE page. **BIT DEPTH** (4 to 16 bits) is on the SENDS page.

### Make an LFO move a setting

An LFO is a slow wave that moves a setting, such as the volume. Each such setting is a destination. Start on a sample instrument.

1. Press `F4` (**MOD**). The header shows the destination, such as **DEST 1/6 Volume**.
2. Press `F4` again to move to the next of the six destinations.
3. Press `Down` to **SOURCE** and turn the encoder to **LFO**. The rows **LFO SHAPE**, **LFO SPEED** and **LFO AMOUNT** appear.
4. Hold a pad. For Volume, that is a tremolo at the tempo's rate.

You should see the shape under the rows. **LFO SHAPE**, **LFO SPEED**, **LFO AMOUNT** and **SOURCE** are heard at once on a held pad: the sound changes within a block, with no wait for the release.

**LFO SPEED** has 29 tempo-sync values, from `128 steps` to `1/64 step`. The Volume destination has the last 24, from `24 steps`.

A destination the instrument does not use is dimmed, not hidden, and the info line says why: `WAVETABLE OR GRANULAR` (the **WT Position** destination on another play mode), `GRANULAR ONLY`, `FILTER OFF` or `SOURCE OFF: PICK ENVELOPE OR LFO`. A dim row can still be edited.

The LFOs of volume, pan, fine tune, cutoff and grain position also run while the transport is stopped, at the rate the tempo gives. Press `Play` with a pad held and the LFO goes on from where it is, with no jump.

The picture is a window of 16 steps (the label `16 STEPS` above it, the axis under it counts steps), so turning **LFO SPEED** changes it at once. At **16 steps** it shows one cycle, at **4 steps** four cycles, at **1 step** sixteen. A slower LFO shows only the start of its cycle: at **128 steps** (DEST 3/6, Cutoff) you see an eighth of it, a slow ramp. The volume LFO starts at 24 steps. Past 32 cycles (faster than **1/2 step**) the cycles are too small to read, so the picture is a filled band between the lowest and the highest level the shape reaches. **Random** shows made-up levels, one for each period; the real LFO picks its own. This picture is new in this firmware.

**LFO SHAPE** has six waves: Rev Saw, Saw, Triangle, Square, Random and **Sine**. Sine is new in this firmware and is not on the original firmware. It is a smooth wave that rises from nothing to the amount at the middle of the period and falls back, and it works like the others: the same speeds, the same amount, all six destinations, and it can be changed while a note sounds. If you export to the original firmware's format, a Sine LFO is written as Triangle and the export page lists it as **SINE LFO**.

### Move a setting with a wavetable envelope or LFO

New in this firmware: **SOURCE** has two more words after **LFO**, **WT Env** and **WT LFO**. They move a destination along one of the 256 wavetable contours instead of an ADSR or a plain LFO shape. Instruments that do not use them are unchanged, and they load and save as before.

1. Press `F4` (**MOD**) and move to a destination with `F4`, such as Panning.
2. On **SOURCE** turn the encoder up past **LFO**: first **WT Env**, then **WT LFO**. Each click is one undo step.
3. **WT Env** has eight rows: **SOURCE**, **WAVE**, **DURATION**, **WARP X**, **WARP Y**, **SUSTAIN**, **RELEASE** and **AMOUNT** (the amplitude destination has no **AMOUNT** row: seven rows). **WAVE** picks the contour, `F001` to `F128` and `U001` to `U128`. **DURATION** is 0.002 to 20.000 s in clicks of 10 ms. A change is heard from the next note, also when the pattern is stopped. The first time a destination switches to WT, **WAVE** may show an older shape number (`F001` to `F006`): turn it to pick the contour you want. **WARP X** and **WARP Y** bend the contour, from -7 to +7. **SUSTAIN** is `OFF` or 1 to 99 %.
4. `F8` (**UNDO**) takes back the last change of one of these rows and nothing else.
5. **WT LFO** has six rows: **SOURCE**, **WAVE**, **LFO SPEED**, **WARP X**, **WARP Y** and **LFO AMOUNT**. **WAVE** and the two warps are the same values as on **WT Env**: a destination keeps one of each.

A change on these rows is heard from the next note, not on a note that is held. These rows cannot be bound to a MIDI controller. Turn **SOURCE** back to **LFO** and the **LFO SHAPE** row reads **Triangle**, whatever contour was set before.

The plot above the rows draws the contour: **WT Env** over its **DURATION** (the length in milliseconds is written above the right edge), **WT LFO** over one cycle. **WARP X** and **WARP Y** bend the picture as they bend the sound, so you can see what the contour does before you play it.

On a **Granular** instrument the fourth destination is **Gran Length**, the grain length, instead of **WT Position**: the header and the rows follow the play mode, and the same **SOURCE** words work on it. Switch the play mode in the editor and the destination keeps its source. An instrument loaded from an older project or an official firmware file that has a source on this destination while it is Granular shows **Off** there, because that source was meant for **WT Position**; set it again to use it as the grain length. The grain length source is a Community OS feature: an export for the official firmware does not carry it.

### Use your own contours from the card

New in this firmware: the 128 user contours `U001` to `U128` can come from WAV files. Without files they hold the built-in shapes, so nothing changes until you add some.

1. On the card, make a folder called `Envelopes` at the top level and put WAV files in it, named by number: `001.wav` is `U001`, `002.wav` is `U002`, up to `128.wav`. `1.wav` works too.
2. Put the card in, or open a project. The files are read then, never while you play. The strip says how it went, for example `ENVELOPES: 12 LOADED`.
3. Pick `U001` (or the number you used) on **WAVE** of a **WT Env** or **WT LFO** row. The plot shows your contour.

The rules for the files:

- The file is PCM, 8, 16 or 24 bit. A stereo file uses its left channel. Float WAV files are refused and counted as `FLOAT` on the strip.
- Any length up to 24,576 frames (0.55 s at 44.1 kHz) is stretched or squeezed to 128 points. A longer file is skipped.
- A file that goes below zero is read as a wave from -1 to 1 and moved into 0 to 1. A file that stays at or above zero is used as it is.
- Numbering starts at 1. If the folder has a `000.wav` or a `0.wav`, it starts at 0 instead: `000.wav` is `U001` and `127.wav` is `U128`. A number past `U128` is skipped.
- A number with no file keeps its built-in contour. A file that cannot be read is skipped (`SKIPPED` on the strip) and the other files still load. If a file is gone the next time (another card, a deleted file), its contour goes back to the built-in one (`RESET`).

A note that is already playing may keep the old shape until its next note. If you change the files while a project is loaded, a slot with a warp on its WT row keeps the old contour until you load the project again.

### Make a MIDI instrument

Start on an empty slot.

1. Press `F2` (**MIDI**). The MIDI page opens with the row **CHANNEL**. Slots 1 to 48 start on channel 1; slots 49 to 64 start on the slot number minus 48.
2. Turn the encoder to set **CHANNEL**, from 1 to 16.
3. Hold a pad. The pad sends a note on that channel instead of playing a sound.

The other rows move one a click, `Shift` makes a coarse step, `Delete` puts the default, and each turn is one undo step. They stop at their ends.

| Row | Range (default) | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| **VELOCITY** | 1 to 127 (127) | The default velocity of its notes. |
| **PROGRAM** | **NONE**, 0 to 127 | Sends a Program Change on the channel when you edit it, and once before the first note after a project load.  |
| **OUT** | **Config**, **DIN**, **USB**, **DIN + USB** (**Config**) | The port the notes and CCs go to. **Config** follows the MIDI OUT port of Config.  |
| **PB RANGE** | 0 to 24 semitones (2) | Turns the Micro-tune FX into a pitch bend; 0 sends none. The PIANO bend strip of the Pattern pads sends -2 to +2 semitones of bend scaled by this range: at 2 the outer pads are the full range.  |
| **OFFSET** | 0 to 100 ms (0) | Delays the notes of this instrument. The length of a note is unchanged.  |

Press `F2` (**CC**) for the controller page: six rows **CC A** to **CC F**, all **CONFIG** (the number set on the Config page) at first. `F1` and `F2` switch between the two pages. Turn a row through `CC 0` to `CC 127`, then **PROG**, **CH AT** and **POLY AT**.  A step FX then sends the slot. With CC A at `CC 74`, CC B at **PROG**, CC C at **CH AT** and CC D at **POLY AT**, FX 8, 9, 10 and 11 send a controller, a Program Change, channel aftertouch and key aftertouch. **POLY AT** sends nothing when no note sounds. FX 37 sends **CC F**, not a Program Change; to send a Program Change, set a slot to **PROG**.

Notes end cleanly. If you change **CHANNEL** or **OUT** while a pad is held, the release goes to the channel and port of its note on. `F7`, `Stop` and a project load end a held note the same way.  A MIDI instrument shows its own page whatever page the instrument beside it was left on.

### Copy, paste and delete an instrument

Start on a sample or MIDI instrument. (On a module instrument `Shift` + `F2` is **MIX**, not COPY: it opens the page with the module's PANNING, DELAY SEND and REVERB SEND.)

1. Press `Shift` + `F2` (**COPY**). The strip says `INS 05 COPIED`.
2. Go to another slot and press `Shift` + `F3` (**PASTE**). The slot becomes a copy: its name, play mode and settings. A used slot is replaced; `F8` gives the old one back.
3. To delete an instrument, press `Shift` + `F4` (**DELETE**).

With nothing copied, **PASTE** is dim and the strip says `NOTHING TO PASTE: SHIFT+F2 COPIES`.  Over a module instrument the strip says `INS 15 IS A MODULE: DELETE IT FIRST` and nothing changes; delete the module, then paste.  `F8` after a paste, and `Shift` + `F8` after that, carry the sound too: the slot is emptied and silenced, or the replaced instrument comes back with its own sound.

> **Careful**: `Shift` + `F4` deletes at once and asks nothing. `F8` (**UNDO**) brings the instrument back with its sample.

### Rename an instrument

Start on a used instrument.

1. Press `Shift` + `F1` (**NAME**). The on-screen keyboard opens with the title **INSTRUMENT NAME**.
2. Type the name with the pads, up to 32 characters.
3. Press `F1` (**OK**) to keep it. `F8` (**CANCEL**) keeps the old name.

You should see `INS 05 RENAMED - F8 UNDO` in the strip.

### Reset an instrument to its defaults

1. Press `Shift` + `Delete`.

You should see `INS 05 INIT - F8 UNDO`. Every row goes back to its default. The name, sample and start and end points stay.

### Save and load an instrument file

1. On a sample instrument, press `Shift` + `F5` (**SAVE**). The strip runs `SAVE <name>` up to 100 %, then **DONE**.
2. The file is `instruments/<NAME>.pti`. A second save never replaces the first; it becomes, for example, `KICK 2.pti`.
   A **STEREO** instrument is saved as its mid, the mix of its two sides, in an ordinary mono `.pti` (the format has no place for the side signal), and the strip says **STEREO: MID WRITTEN, SIDE NOT KEPT**. A project export to the OG folder counts such instruments as **STEREO** among the things it leaves out.
3. To load a file, press `F5` (**LOAD**) on an empty slot. Sample load shows the `.pti` files.
4. Move the cursor to a file and press `F1` (**LOAD**). The Instrument screen comes back on the slot, with the instrument and its sound.

A saved file loads again as the same instrument: every page shows the same values and the two sound the same. The file is in the original firmware's instrument format. Whether an official unit takes it is not checked.  A load refuses a file that is not an instrument or is cut short, and one with stereo-length audio, no audio, or no room in the sample memory. The strip says why (`UNKNOWN FILE TYPE`, `TRUNCATED`, `UNSUPPORTED FORMAT`, `NO AUDIO IN THE FILE`, `THE SAMPLE ARENA IS FULL`), and the slot is untouched.

The save goes to any SD card you can write to. On a write-protected card the strip says **CARD IS WRITE PROTECTED** and nothing is created.

## Keys on this screen

The key row, and the row drawn while `Shift` is held. `-` means the key does nothing.

| Key | Label | With `Shift` |
|---|---|---|
| `F1` | **SAMPLE** | **NAME** |
| `F2` | **VOICE** | **COPY** |
| `F3` | **FILTER** | **PASTE** |
| `F4` | **MOD** | **DELETE** |
| `F5` | **SENDS** | **SAVE** |
| `F6` | **<INS** | **<USED** |
| `F7` | **INS>** | **USED>** |
| `F8` | **UNDO** | **REDO** |

Three labels in the table are the ones the screen starts with, and they change as you work. `F1` follows the instrument: **SAMPLE**, **SLICE**, **WT** or **GRAIN** on a sample instrument (by its play mode), **MIDI** on a MIDI instrument, and the module's own page names on a module instrument, where `F5` is **PRESET**: it opens the module's list of presets (see [Modules and apps](modules.md)).  `F6` and `F7` show the numbers next to the instrument in view, such as `<06` and `08>`, and are dim where there is none. While `Shift` is held they show the nearest instruments that are in use.

| Key | What it does | Ref |
|---|---|---|
| `Params` | Opens the Instrument screen. Pressed again, it goes to the first page. | QA-INS-011 |
| `F1` (**SAMPLE**, **SLICE**, **WT** or **GRAIN**) | The source page of a sample instrument. The label follows the play mode. On a MIDI instrument, the MIDI page. | QA-INS-005, QA-INS-061 |
| `F2` (**VOICE**) | The VOICE page, with the VEL> row. | QA-INS-082 |
| `F3` (**FILTER**) | The FILTER page, with the CUTOFF row. | QA-INS-085 |
| `F4` (**MOD**) | The MOD page: a SOURCE row (Off, Envelope, LFO, WT Env, WT LFO) and the rows of the source you pick, for each destination. Pressed again, it moves to the next of the six destinations. | QA-INS-035, QA-INS-010, QA-INS-294 |
| `F5` (**SENDS**) | The SENDS page, with the OVERDRIVE row. | QA-INS-002 |
| `F6` (**<NN**) | The previous instrument, such as `<06`. Dim at 1. | QA-INS-007 |
| `F7` (**NN>**) | The next instrument, such as `02>`. Dim at 64. | QA-INS-007 |
| `F8` (**UNDO**) | Takes back the last instrument change. | QA-INS-040 |
| `Shift` + `F1` (**NAME**) | Renames the instrument. | QA-INS-050 |
| `Shift` + `F2` (**COPY**) | Copies the instrument. On a module instrument it is **MIX** and opens the pan and sends page; pressing it again goes back. | QA-INS-043, QA-INS-307 |
| `Shift` + `F3` (**PASTE**) | Pastes the copy into the slot. | QA-INS-044, QA-INS-045 |
| `Shift` + `F4` (**DELETE**) | Deletes the instrument at once. | QA-INS-030 |
| `Shift` + `F5` (**SAVE**) | Saves a sample instrument as a `.pti` file. | QA-INS-052, QA-INS-054 |
| `Shift` + `F6` (**<USED**), `Shift` + `F7` (**USED>**) | Go to the nearest instrument in use. | QA-INS-009 |
| `Shift` + `F8` (**REDO**) | Does the last undone change again. | QA-INS-001 |
| `Shift` + `Delete` | Sets every row to its default. | QA-INS-032 |
| `Delete` | Puts the row under the cursor back to its default. | QA-INS-021, QA-INS-064 |
| `Up`, `Down` | Move the cursor between the rows. | QA-INS-010 |
| `Left`, `Right` | Change the value under the cursor by one click of the encoder, down or up. A held arrow repeats, and one `F8` takes the whole run back. The empty slot's type chooser keeps its old use. | QA-INS-222, QA-INS-024 |
| `Shift` + `Left`, `Shift` + `Right` | A coarse step, as `Shift` + encoder. | QA-INS-223 |
| encoder | Changes the value under the cursor. | QA-INS-019, QA-INS-085 |
| `Shift` + encoder | A coarse step. On CHANNEL, each click moves four. | QA-INS-064 |
| pad | Plays the instrument in view. On a MIDI instrument it sends a note. | QA-INS-013, QA-INS-033 |
| `Shift` + pad | Plays the instrument in view, as a pad alone does, so you can hold `Shift` for a coarse step and tap pads together. It does not change the instrument: use `F6` and `F7`, or `Shift` + `F6` and `Shift` + `F7`. New Community OS behaviour. | QA-INS-012 |

## Good to know

- On a sample instrument `F1` to `F5` pick the pages SOURCE, VOICE, FILTER, MOD and SENDS. Press the key of the page you are on again to step through that key's windows: on MOD, `F4` walks the six destinations. `Left` and `Right` change the value, and `Up` and `Down` move between rows. A MIDI instrument has two pages: **MIDI** on `F1` and **CC** on `F2`.
- Most settings change a note that is already playing: volume, tune, fine tune, pan, cutoff, resonance, drive, bit depth, the envelopes, the LFO settings and the loop points. Not live: PCM, the start and end, the slices, the loop mode, and the voices of the Amiga engine, which read their settings when a note starts. Glide applies from the next note.
- An empty slot has no parameter rows. It shows the type chooser: `F1` **SAMPLE**, `F2` **MIDI**, `F3` **PASTE** (dim until you copy an instrument), `F4` **MODULE** (opens the engine picker: `F1` **SELECT**, `F8` **BACK**) and `F5` **LOAD**. A load makes the instrument anew. `F1` opens Sample load aimed at this slot, and the Instrument screen comes back on it after the load.
- On an empty slot `Shift` shows `<10`, the nearest instrument in use, and `USED>` is dim when none follows. **NAME** to **SAVE** are dim, and so is **PASTE** while nothing is copied.
- Change instrument with `F7` or `Stop` and a held note ends on the instrument that started it. A pad released later is silent.
- Any row with a value can sit on the encoder: put the cursor on it and open Learn with `Vol` and `Fx` and press `F7` (**ENC**), then hold `Instr` and `Vol` and turn the encoder from any screen. See [Put one parameter on the encoder](panel.md#put-one-parameter-on-the-encoder).
- A MIDI CC learned on a parameter, such as the cutoff, is one undo step for the whole sweep. `F8` on the Instrument screen brings the value back.
- A project saved with MIDI fields opens in an older build with the instrument whole and the twelve MIDI fields at their defaults.
- A row that does not apply is dimmed, and the info line says why.
- WAVETABLE needs a sample of at least 32 frames. A shorter one is refused.
- A wavetable window bigger than the sample is not drawn, and the instrument is silent.
- A WT Position LFO moves while the transport is stopped. Not checked against the original firmware.
- A MIDI instrument has no VOICE, FILTER, MOD or SENDS page. Pressing those keys says so.
- A pasted copy keeps its sound after the source is deleted.
- Checked on the unit (build 0.4.18): the MIDI channel, MIDI notes, and `Shift` + `F4` with its undo.

## See also

- [Pattern](pattern.md): the notes that play an instrument.
- [Wave and Chop](wave.md): the sample, its slices and its wavetable.
- [Sample load](sample_load.md): loading a sample or a `.pti` file into a slot.
- [Modules and apps](modules.md): module instruments.

---

# App pages

Status: draft

Every app, such as MIDI Monitor or Rhythm Gen, draws its own page, and the OS keeps the same frame around it: the strip on top, an info line, and a key row with `F8` (**BACK**) last. `Play` is always the transport's, and a screen button leaves the app for its own screen. This is new in track3r-os, and so are apps.  What each app does is in [Modules](modules.md); this page covers what every app page shares.

## What it is for

Use this page to find your way around any app. You open an app from the **MODULES** screen with `F1`, or from Pattern: `F7` (**TOOLS**), then `F1` runs the app. You leave it with `F8`.

## The screen at a glance

| Area | What it shows |
|---|---|
| Strip | `APP`, the transport, `NAME midimon`, `STATE RUNNING` and the CPU and memory readout. If the unit stopped the app, `STATE STOPPED`. |
| Main area | The app's own pane, such as the rows of **MIDI MONITOR** at the bottom. If the unit stopped the app, **APP STOPPED**. |
| Info line | `the app has the input` on the left and `F8: back` on the right. |
| Key row | The app's own labels, `F8` **BACK** last. An app that declares none reads `--` on `F1` to `F7`. |

## More tasks

### Go back to where you opened the app

Start on an app page.

1. Press `F8` (**BACK**), or `F7` and `F8` together.

You return to where you came from. An app opened from Pattern brings you back to Pattern, with the cursor and the block as they were. An app opened from **MODULES** brings you back to **MODULES**. The app is ended, and there is one level of return.

### Leave for another screen

1. Press a screen button, such as `Song` or `Pattern`.

The screen of the button opens and the app is ended. The app never hears the press or the release. All eleven screen buttons do the same.

### Start and stop the transport

1. Press `Play`. The transport starts or stops, and the transport mark in the strip follows.

The page stays and the app does not see `Play`. `Rec`, the pads and the other keys still reach the app.

### Read the help page

1. Press `Shift` + `Config`. **HELP: MODULE APP** opens over the app, page 15 of 15, and the key row reads `F8` **CLOSE**.
2. Press `F8`. The app page is back, and the app kept running.

The page lists `F8` BACK, `Play`, `Shift` + `Config`, `Shift` + `Up` and `Down`, `Shift` + encoder, `Shift` + `Delete` and `Shift` + `F8`, which does nothing. While it is up, the app gets the press and release of `Shift` only, and nothing else.

### Edit the parameters of an older app

An app built for a module ABI (the version of the interface between the OS and a module) below 1.10 may declare parameters. The OS then draws a **PARAMETERS** column on the left. The example app Pads is one. Start on such an app.

1. Press `Shift` + `Down` and `Shift` + `Up` to move the selected row.
2. Turn the encoder with `Shift` held to change the value of the row. The app hears the change.
3. Press `Shift` + `Delete` to put the row back to its default.

The app is given none of these keys. An app that declares no parameter, or is of ABI 1.10, has no such column. It gets every Shift key and uses them for its own coarse steps: in Rhythm Gen, `Shift` + encoder moves four steps a detent.

## Keys on this screen

| Key | What it does | Ref |
|---|---|---|
| `F8` (**BACK**), `F7` and `F8` together | Leave the app for where it was opened. | QA-APP-002 |
| A screen button | Ends the app and opens that screen. | QA-APP-003 |
| `Shift` + `Config` | Opens the help page of the app page. | QA-APP-004 |
| `Shift` + `Up`, `Shift` + `Down` | Select a row of the OS column of parameters. | QA-APP-005 |
| `Shift` + encoder | Edits the selected parameter. | QA-APP-006 |
| `Shift` + `Delete` | Puts the selected parameter back to its default. | QA-APP-007 |
| Any Shift key, on an app without the column | Goes to the app. | QA-APP-008 |
| `Play` | The transport's. | QA-APP-009 |

## Good to know

- The parameter column exists only for an app below ABI 1.10 that declares a parameter. Pads is the only one shipped; the simulator's card does not hold it.
- What a press at the first or last row of the column does is not checked.

## See also

- [Modules](modules.md): installing modules and what each bundled app does.
- [Pattern](pattern.md): the **TOOLS** list that launches an app.

---

# Pattern

Status: draft

Pattern has three record modes where the official firmware has one edit switch: `Rec` turns step entry on, and `Shift` + `Rec` turns live recording on. While a pattern plays you hold `F1` and pick another pattern, which takes over at the next step with no stop. A zoom shows up to 12 tracks.  The pad layouts of the `Shift` row, such as a piano or a pattern picker, the quarter jumps and blocks of single columns are new in track3r-os.

## What it is for

Use Pattern to write the notes of the current pattern, live or one step at a time, and to copy, delete and undo parts of it. Open it with the `Pattern` button. A **step** is one row of the grid, and a **track** is one column group; see the [glossary](glossary.md). A pattern has 16 tracks. The zoom shows 5, 8 or 12 of them: hold `Note` and tap `Instr` to change it. Each track has columns for the note, the instrument, the volume and two effects.

## How it works

The notes are stored: they live in the pattern, and they are saved with the project. What you do not store is the **record mode**, the answer to "what do the pads and `Play` do to the pattern right now?" The chip in the info line shows it.

- **WATCH** is the browse mode. Pads only preview the sound, and nothing is written.
- **STEP** writes each pad you press on the cursor's step, then moves the cursor on by **JUMP**. The playhead does not move the cursor. `Rec` turns it on and off.
- **LIVE** writes the pads you play at the playhead while the pattern plays, and the view follows the playhead. `Shift` + `Rec` turns it on and off, from any mode, and so do `Rec` and then `Play`, tapped within a few hundredths of a second. Turning LIVE off takes you back to the mode you turned it on from, STEP or WATCH.

Only a key press ends a mode, with one exception: when the song ends in LIVE, the chip goes back to WATCH and the take ends. STEP stays.  In STEP and LIVE a red frame shows that the pattern can be edited. The buttons have no lights, so the chip and the red frame are the signs.

An example: press `Rec`, then pads 1, 5, 8 and 12. Four notes sit on four steps in a row, and the cursor waits on the fifth. Press `Rec` again: the chip reads WATCH, and the notes stay. A whole LIVE take is one undo step.

## Try it

Start with a new project. To hear the notes, put a sample on instrument 1 (see [Sample load](sample_load.md)).

1. Press `Pattern`. The grid opens in **WATCH**.
2. Press `Rec`. The chip reads **STEP**, and a red frame shows.
3. Press pad 1, pad 5, pad 8 and pad 12. Each note is written on the cursor's step, and the cursor moves on.

   (Picture: Pattern, STEP mode: four notes on four steps in a row, and the cursor on the fifth step.)

4. Press `Play`. The header reads **PLAY**, and a green bar, the playhead, runs down the steps. The cursor stays put, and you hear the four notes if instrument 1 has a sample.

   (Picture: Pattern while it plays: the header reads PLAY, a green bar marks the playhead, and the cursor stays on step 5.)

5. Press `Play` to stop, then `Rec`. The chip reads **WATCH**, and the four notes stay.

   (Picture: Pattern, WATCH mode, stopped: the chip reads WATCH and the four notes are still in the grid.)

## The screen at a glance

(Picture: Pattern, STEP mode with the pattern stopped: the chip reads STEP and the red frame shows that the pattern can be edited.)

| Area | What it shows |
|---|---|
| Track headers | The number and name of each track, with its MUTE and SOLO tags. |
| Grid | One row per step. Each track has the columns **Note**, **Instr**, **Vol** and **Fx**. The cursor row is always the 8th of the 16 rows, also on the first and last step; the rows past the ends are blank.  |
| Info line | The record mode chip (**WATCH**, **STEP** or **LIVE**) at the left edge, then the scale and the track, the pattern name such as `P01 intro`, and the pads' mode (`pads NOTES`, `pads TRACKS` and so on). A **METRO** chip and the hint for a block come after them, and `undo` and its depth stand at the right edge. |
| Key row | `F1` to `F8`. `F1` to `F3` are **PATTERN**, **LENGTH** and **JUMP**. |
| Shift row | The labels drawn while `Shift` is held: the pad octave and layouts. |

## More tasks

### Record a part into a playing pattern

Start on the Pattern screen, in WATCH. The pattern can be stopped or playing.

(Picture: Panel: Shift is ringed and Rec is marked. Hold Shift, then press Rec to turn LIVE on or off.)

1. Press `Shift` + `Rec`. The chip reads **LIVE**, in red. A stopped transport starts now, after the count-in when COUNT-IN is on.
2. Play the pads. The notes are written at the playhead. The cursor follows it, and the view keeps the playing row in the middle.
3. Press `Shift` + `Rec` to turn LIVE off: the chip goes back to STEP if you came from STEP, and to WATCH if you came from WATCH. `Rec` always goes to WATCH. `Play` stops the transport and ends the take.

You should see the new notes in the grid.

### Record knob moves as FX

A knob that MIDI Learn bound to an instrument parameter also writes into the pattern while you record LIVE: each move becomes a step FX on the play line of the cursor's track. CUTOFF records as Low-, High- or Band-pass (27 / 28 / 29, by the instrument's FILTER TYPE), and PANNING, DELAY SEND, REVERB SEND, OVERDRIVE and BIT DEPTH record as their own FX (31, 30, 32, 38, 39). The FX goes to the column that already holds one of the same group, else to the first free column; another FX is never overwritten, and when both columns are taken the strip says **REC FX: NO FREE FX COLUMN**. At the take's first recorded FX the strip says **REC FX: CUTOFF** — the parameter's name. One value per step: a later move on the same step overwrites it, and the step's note, instrument and volume stay as they are. Only a binding of the selected instrument records, and only while the pattern records LIVE (not in STEP, stopped, during the count-in, or with the playhead in another pattern). One Undo takes the whole take back, notes and FX together, and the instrument parameter stays where the knob left it. The encoder target (see [Put one parameter on the encoder](panel.md#put-one-parameter-on-the-encoder)) records the same way, and also in STEP, on the cursor's step; a row that has neither an FX nor a letter (below) says **REC FX: <name> HAS NO FX**. Outside a LIVE take a knob move changes nothing in the pattern. New in track3r-os.

A parameter with no FX of its own, such as VOLUME or TUNE, records as a CC letter, **CC A** to **CC F**. The first recorded move takes the first free letter of the project, and the strip says **REC FX: VOLUME -> CC A**; the same parameter keeps its letter, the next one takes the next. Six letters are the limit: a seventh parameter says **REC FX: NO FREE CC LETTER**, still sounds, and is not recorded. A track whose instrument is a MIDI one says **REC FX: MIDI TRACK** and nothing is written. One Undo takes the step and its letter back together. When the pattern plays, the letter moves that parameter and sends no MIDI; playing it does not change the project (it stays saved, a save during playback works), and at stop the parameter returns to its saved value. An export does not render these moves and says **CC LETTER MOVES NOT RENDERED**. New in track3r-os.

The exception is a MIDI instrument with REC STORE set to Lane: the CC A to CC F rows of that instrument do not write a step FX or change their controller number; each move goes into the lane as the controller the letter names (see "New in track3r-os" above).

### Select a block

Start in STEP, WATCH (stopped or playing) or LIVE. A block is the steps and tracks you mark. Inside one track it can be just some columns: note with instrument (they go together), volume, FX1, FX2.

(Picture: Panel: Shift is ringed and the four arrow keys are marked. Hold Shift, then press an arrow to select a block.)

1. Hold `Shift` and press `Down`, `Up`, `Left` or `Right`. The block is highlighted from the cursor.
2. Keep `Shift` and an arrow to extend the block.
3. To mark columns, put the cursor on the first column you want, then hold `Shift` and press `Down` (more steps) or `Left` or `Right` (one column at a time).
4. To select a whole column fast, put the cursor on step 1 in `Instr`, `Vol`, `FX1` or `FX2` and hold `Shift` while you press `Up`. The first press marks that column over every step of the track. A second press marks the whole track, and a third marks every track. On the `Note` column the first press already marks the whole track.

You should see the block over the steps and tracks you chose, and over just the columns you chose while it stays in one track. Over several tracks the cursor's track keeps the bright blue and the other tracks of the block are a slightly duller blue, so you can see which track the cursor is in.  `Shift` + `Right` past the last column takes the next track whole; from there `Shift` + `Left` or `Right` add or drop a whole track at a time.  The playhead does not move it. While the view follows the playhead (WATCH playing, LIVE) the block starts at the step the playhead is on at your first arrow press, and the cursor stays on the playhead.  `Delete` clears the highlighted columns and closes the block: every column for whole steps, only the note and instrument for a block in the Note column. `Shift` + `Insert` or a plain arrow also closes it. With a block on the `Instr`, `Vol`, `FX1` or `FX2` column, the encoder (and `Shift` + encoder) changes that column's values inside the block and nothing outside it.  The one-column block stays when you let go of `Shift`; `Shift` + `Down` from it makes a block of whole steps again.

### Loop a block (Focus Loop)

New in track3r-os. Start in STEP, WATCH or LIVE, with a block selected (see "Select a block").

1. Press `Shift` + `Play`. The pattern starts on the first step of the block and plays to its last step, then goes back to the first step, again and again. It never counts in.
2. If the pattern is already playing, `Shift` + `Play` does the same: the play line jumps to the first step of the block and the loop begins.
3. To stop, press `Play`, or `Shift` + `Play` again.

You should see **LOOP 05-12  PLAY: STOP** on the info line while it loops (the step numbers follow the **NUMBERING** setting). The block stays selected. With no block, `Shift` + `Play` plays from the step under the cursor and does not loop. A track shorter than the pattern plays its own steps inside the loop, and changing the pattern or stopping ends the loop.

### Copy and paste steps

Start in STEP, with a block selected or with only the cursor on a step.

1. Press `Copy`. The strip says **COPIED n STEPS**, or **COPIED 1 STEP** with no block. Nothing changes.
2. Move the cursor to the new place.
3. Press `Shift` + `Copy`. The copy is written with its top-left step on the cursor.

You should see the copied steps. A block of columns copies and pastes those columns only, in the same columns; the other columns under it stay.  The clip stays, so you can paste it again. Pasting past the last step or track cuts the rest. There is no cut key: copy, then delete.  New in track3r-os: a block of whole steps (two or more tracks, or all the columns) also carries the MIDI lane events of its tracks and rows, and the whole-pattern clip carries every track's; a paste replaces the lane events under it in the same undo, and Delete on a selected block takes them too. A paste the lane memory cannot take is refused whole (**LANES DO NOT FIT: NOTHING CHANGED**), and a block of more than 2,048 lane events copies its steps only (**NO LANES: TOO MANY**). Insert and Shift + Delete of rows move the lane events with the rows.  In WATCH the copy works, but the paste writes nothing and the strip says **TURN EDIT ON**. A whole-pattern clip (the `F1` row of the keys table) pastes the steps, the lane events and the track lengths; the name stays the target's.  Fill, the TOOLS list (DUPLICATE, EXPAND, SHRINK), the tool apps and EXPORT SELECTION always take whole steps. With a block of columns, Fill and DUPLICATE say **WHOLE STEPS** in the strip.

> **Careful**: Paste writes over the steps under it. One `F8` (**UNDO**) takes it back.

### Delete and pull steps

Start in STEP, with the cursor on a step.

1. Press `Delete`. The step under the cursor is cleared, and the cursor moves on by **JUMP**.
2. Hold `Shift` and press `Delete`. The steps below move up over the step under the cursor, and the cursor moves on by **JUMP** like `Delete` does (it stops on the last row; with JUMP 0 it stays).
3. Press `Insert`, then `Shift` + `Delete`. The pattern is as it was before.

Holding `Delete` clears one step after another; each is one undo step.

### Change values in big steps

`Shift` + turn the encoder moves in big steps; the plain encoder moves one step.

| Where the cursor is | `Shift` + encoder, one detent |
|---|---|
| **Note** column | one octave |
| **Instr** column | 8 instruments (1 to 64) |
| **Vol** column | 10 (0 to 127) |
| **Fx** value | 16 |
| Browse (WATCH) | one page of 16 rows |

The values stop at their first and last entry. The **PATTERN**, **LENGTH** and **JUMP** choosers (hold `F1` to `F3`) move eight places a detent.

### Switch to another pattern while it plays

Start on the Pattern screen, with the transport playing. Use this to go from a verse to a break without a stop.

1. Hold `F1`. The strip shows **PATTERN** and the number in view. The pads light as in PATS: the playing pattern is bright, one with notes is dim, an empty one is dark.
2. Holding `F1`, press a pad (pad 1 is pattern 1, up to 48), turn the encoder, or press `Up` or `Down`. `Left` and `Right` jump to the previous and next pattern that exists, skipping unused numbers. `Shift` + encoder moves eight patterns.
3. Let go of `F1`. The strip closes. The new pattern loops.

The playing pattern changes at the next step and goes on at the same row. Notes still sounding end. The last pick wins, and picking the pattern that plays takes back a pick that has not landed. An empty pattern works too: the strip says **EMPTY**, and nothing is created until you write a note.  When the song plays, the pick leaves the song and loops your pattern (**LEAVES THE SONG**); press `Play` to stop, then `Play` on the Song screen to start the song again.  When the transport is stopped or counting in, the pick only chooses the pattern to view and edit.

In LIVE the take goes on, and a note you play between the pick and the next step is refused with **THE PLAYHEAD IS IN ANOTHER PATTERN**. In PATS (`Shift` + `F6`) a pad queues the pattern for the end of the one that plays.  The official firmware also switches while one plays, at once, with the `Pattern` button held. Here the held `F1` does it, at the next step.  With PAT SWITCH on **Pattern end** (Config, PATTERN page), a pick in the held `F1` chooser waits for the end of the pattern, as a PATS pad does: the pick is queued, the view follows the playing pattern once you let go, and the same pad again takes the queue back.

### Show more tracks at once

The zoom cycles from 5 tracks to 8 and then to 12, and back to 5. Every level shows the same 16 rows, and the cursor row stays in the middle.  At the 5-track zoom an FX cell reads the effect's three capitals, such as `CHD`, `ARP` or `SLD`, with its value after them; the 8 and 12 zooms draw no FX.

(Picture: Panel: Note is ringed. Instr is marked ZOOM, and Left and Right are marked TRACK. Hold Note, then press one of them.)

1. Hold `Note`, tap `Instr`, then let both go. The zoom changes.
2. Hold `Note` and press `Right` or `Left` to move the cursor one whole track. Hold the arrow to repeat.

A tap of `Note` selects the Note column; a hold of half a second opens the Note popup.

### Choose the key: hold `Note`

Start on the Pattern screen. Hold `Note` for half a second: the **NOTE ENTRY** panel opens, and its top line names the key in force.

1. Turn the encoder, or press `Up` or `Down`, to step through all 39 keys, one a detent, wrapping at both ends.
2. Or press a pad of the second pad row: it holds twelve of the keys. For any of the other 27 no pad of the row is lit.

You should see the top line name the key at every step, for example `C Hirajoshi - Jump 1 - Oct 3 - Lock off`, and the info line read `scale Hirajoshi C-4`.  Turn **SCALE LOCK** on (the last pad) and the pads and a MIDI keyboard snap to the key: a C# played in is written as the C of the key.  The key is saved with the project: save, switch the unit off and on, open the project again, and the panel opens on the same key.  A new project starts in **C Major**, so the pads light the notes of the scale at once; pick **Chromatic** (the first pad of the second row) to light every note. A project saved before this version has no key stored and opens in Chromatic, as it did. New in track3r-os.  Two pairs of keys have the same notes (Hung. minor and Gypsy minor, Diminished and Whole-half), and Todi keeps the standard notes of its name here.  The same 39 keys the original firmware lists under its Config's Notes scale are on this panel. New in track3r-os.

### Open the Navigator

The Navigator is the list of screens.

1. Press `Song` and `Pattern` together, or `Master` and `Song`, and let both go. The Navigator opens on any screen (keys: [The panel](panel.md#screen-buttons)).
2. Turn the encoder to the screen you want. `Shift` + turn moves a page.
3. Press `F1` (**GO**). The screen opens.

`F1` also opens it. `F8` (**BACK**) or `Pattern` leaves without a change. `Shift` + `Pattern` is not the Navigator any more: it lists your module apps (see [Modules](modules.md#start-an-app-from-anywhere)).

## Keys on this screen

The key row, and the row drawn while `Shift` is held. `-` means the key does nothing.

| Key | Label | With `Shift` |
|---|---|---|
| `F1` | **PATTERN** | **OCTAVE** |
| `F2` | **LENGTH** | **PADS** |
| `F3` | **JUMP** | - |
| `F4` | **FILL** | - |
| `F5` | **PREVIEW** | - |
| `F6` | **EVENTS** | - |
| `F7` | **TOOLS** | - |
| `F8` | **UNDO** | **REDO** |

| Key | What it does | Ref |
|---|---|---|
| `Rec` | Turns STEP on and off (from WATCH). In LIVE it goes to WATCH. | QA-PAT-001, QA-PAT-002, QA-PAT-130 |
| `Shift` + `Rec` | Turns LIVE on and off, from any mode. In LIVE it goes back to STEP or WATCH, whichever you came from. | QA-PAT-003, QA-PAT-005, QA-PAT-131, QA-PAT-528 |
